# Ramonyx — llms-full (public)

> Full public corpus for agents: public machine layer (JSON) + public documentation.
> Source: repo RamonyxJS/ramonyx (https://ramonyx.devmoon.net). Internal docs are never included.

## Search

This site has a search endpoint: https://context7.com/api/v2/ask?siteKey=ask_89339fd8bad939f239a589fa&query=<URL-encoded question>. It returns documentation that answers the question, with a source link for each part. No API key is needed. If nothing matches, it says so.

Context7 library: https://context7.com/websites/ramonyx_devmoon_net

```json
      "rule": "Tulis TypeScript yang erasable: dilarang `enum`, `namespace`, parameter property, dan `import =`. Tipe harus hilang saat transpile.",
      "rationale": "Paket framework diekspor sebagai `.ts` dan dijalankan Node type stripping (tanpa transpile). Sintaks non-erasable gagal saat runtime.",
      "scope": "framework",
      "good": "export type Status = \"ok\" | \"error\";\nconst STATUS = { ok: \"ok\" } as const;",

      "bad": "import { createApp } from \"./app\";",

      "rationale": "Paket edge-safe harus berjalan di runtime edge/serverless tanpa `node:*` (artefak `--target edge`, ADR-0058); paket Node-only memang butuh fs/net/build.",
```

## docs/public/machine/glossary.json

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "terms": [
    {
      "term": "SSR (Server-Side Rendering)",
      "definition": "Render React di server menjadi HTML; dua mode: sinkron (`renderToString`) dan streaming (opt-in `streaming: true`, `renderToReadableStream`).",
      "related": [
        "Hydration",
        "Streaming SSR"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/api/core-contract.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Streaming SSR",
      "definition": "SSR yang mengirim HTML bertahap; error setelah byte pertama memutus koneksi (status/error page hanya berlaku sebelum byte pertama). Memakai `react-dom/server.edge`.",
      "related": [
        "SSR (Server-Side Rendering)",
        "Suspense"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/engineering/adr/0047-ssr-streaming.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Hydration",
      "definition": "Mengaktifkan React di browser atas HTML SSR: payload inline `window.__RAMONYX__` + satu bundle client + `hydrateRoot`. Halaman error tidak di-hydrate.",
      "related": [
        "SSR (Server-Side Rendering)",
        "Soft navigation"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/engineering/adr/0007-hydration.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Soft navigation",
      "definition": "Navigasi klien tanpa full reload: fetch HTML halaman → swap `#ramonyx-root` → re-hydrate; `document.title` + scroll direset. Belum ada prefetch.",
      "related": [
        "Hydration"
      ]
    },
    {
      "term": "Loader",
      "definition": "Fungsi per halaman yang mengambil data sebelum render (GET, boleh async); hasilnya harus JSON-serializable karena ikut payload hydration.",
      "related": [
        "Page module",
        "Payload"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/api/core-contract.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Page module",
      "definition": "Modul `.tsx` di folder rute yang mengekspor komponen `default` + opsional `load` dan `metadata` (title/status).",
      "related": [
        "Loader",
        "Layout",
        "Route manifest"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/api/core-contract.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Layout",
      "definition": "Komponen pembungkus per folder (`layout.tsx`) yang membungkus halaman; bersarang dan layout terdekat menang.",
      "related": [
        "Page module",
        "Error boundary"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/api/core-contract.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Error boundary",
      "definition": "Komponen `error.tsx` per folder yang dirender saat loader/render gagal; boundary terdekat menang. Halaman error tidak di-hydrate.",
      "related": [
        "Layout"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/api/core-contract.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Route manifest",
      "definition": "Artefak compiler yang memetakan file rute → pola URL, method, dan entry (dibuat saat build/dev; sumber kebenaran routing).",
      "related": [
        "Page module",
        "Route entry"
      ]
    },
    {
      "term": "Route entry",
      "definition": "Pasangan rute halaman/API + handler yang dihasilkan compiler dan dipasang ke pipeline server.",
      "related": [
        "Route manifest"
      ]
    },
    {
      "term": "Middleware",
      "definition": "Fungsi app-level (array di `createHandler`) yang berjalan berurutan sebelum rute; dapat mengganti request (mis. menyuntik nonce). Belum ada per-folder.",
      "related": [
        "Handler",
        "CSP nonce"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/api/core-contract.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Handler",
      "definition": "Pipeline request server: middleware → pencocokan rute → validasi → eksekusi (halaman/API) dengan limits (body/timeout/concurrency).",
      "related": [
        "Middleware",
        "Adapter"
      ]
    },
    {
      "term": "Adapter",
```

## docs/public/machine/cli.json

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedAt": "2026-10-23T04:58:33.613Z",
  "usage": "ramonyx — CLI pengembangan Ramonyx\n\nPemakaian:\n  ramonyx dev              Vite + HMR (default :5173) → SSR (port dari config)\n  ramonyx build            Bundel klien → dist/client (jalankan sebelum start produksi)\n  ramonyx build --static   Bundel klien + prerender halaman → dist/static (hosting statis)\n  ramonyx build --target edge\n                           Bundel server edge/serverless → dist/edge (kontrak fetch handler)\n  ramonyx start            Server produksi (NODE_ENV=production, SSR)\n  ramonyx start --watch    Restart server saat src/** berubah\n  ramonyx add <nama[@versi]> --registry <path|url>\n                           Pasang plugin + verifikasi integritas/signature\n  ramonyx remove <nama>    Hapus plugin + lock entry\n  ramonyx doctor           Diagnostik konfigurasi & lingkungan\n  ramonyx routes           Daftar halaman + route API (manifest)\n  ramonyx check            Periksa config, entry, route, dan batas client/server\n  ramonyx ai               init|sync: AGENTS.md + adapter agen + konfigurasi MCP\n  ramonyx version          Versi CLI\n  ramonyx help             Bantuan ini\n\nOpsi:\n  --app <dir>       Direktori aplikasi (default: direktori kerja saat ini)\n  --config <path>   Path config (default: <app>/ramonyx.config.ts)\n  --port <n>        Override port server SSR\n  --dev-port <n>    Override port Vite (default 5173)\n  --static          (build) Prerender rute statis + getStaticPaths → dist/static\n  --target <nama>   (build) Target: edge | vercel | deno (dist/<target>, fetch handler)\n  --watch           (build/start) Bangun ulang atau restart server saat src/** berubah\n  --registry <path|url>  (add/remove) Registry plugin JSON\n  --public-key <path>     (add) Public key Ed25519 PEM untuk verifikasi signature\n  --agents <list>   (ai) Adapter: claude,cursor,copilot,opencode (default semua)\n  --no-mcp          (ai) Jangan tulis konfigurasi MCP\n  --force           (ai) Timpa berkas yang sudah ada (termasuk AGENTS.md tanpa marker)\n  --dry-run         (ai) Laporkan aksi tanpa menulis\n  --json            (doctor/routes/check/ai) Output JSON yang dapat dibaca mesin\n\nKonvensi:\n  src/app.ts        mengekspor createApp(options?) → FetchHandler\n  src/routes        halaman (page.tsx/layout.tsx/error.tsx) + API (api/*.ts)\n  ramonyx.config.ts default export { app?, server? } (opsional)\n\n",
```

```json
      "title": "Deploy static or edge output",
      "summary": "Prerender static routes or build a fetch-handler bundle, then deploy the generated directory.",
      "when": "You need a CDN/static host or an edge/serverless runtime instead of a Node process.",
      "files": [
        "dist/static",

      ],

    },
```

## docs/public/api/core-contract.md

# API Reference

The public API surface, grouped by package. Everything is ESM, TypeScript-first, and edge-safe
unless noted.

## `ramonyx` (meta package)

Re-exports the common primitives:

```ts
import {
  route, createHandler, HttpError, defineConfig, resolveConfig,
  createCache, createMemoryStore, mergeHooks, formDataToObject,
  createTranslator, negotiateLocale, localePath, parseAcceptLanguage,
} from "ramonyx";
```

## Server — `@ramonyx/server`

```ts
createHandler(options): FetchHandler
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routes` | `RouteEntry[]` | required |
| `middleware` | `Middleware[]` | `[]` |
| `env` | `EnvReader` | `process.env` |
| `logger` | `Logger` | console |
| `strictValidation` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `hooks` | `AppHooks` | — |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | `1_048_576` |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `10_000` |
| `maxConcurrent` | `number` | `100` |
| `envFromRequest` | `(request) => EnvReader?` | — |

Also: `traceId()`, `requestLogging()`, `createMetrics()`, `createMetricsRoute(metrics)`.

## Core — `@ramonyx/core`

```ts
route<Params, Query, Body, Output>({ handler, params?, query?, body?, output? }): RouteDefinition
```

`handler(context)` receives `{ request, params, query, body, env, log, json(), text(), redirect() }`.
Invalid schema input → `400` with `issues`; invalid output → `500`.

Other exports: `HttpError`, `defineConfig`, `resolveConfig`, `mergeHooks`, `formDataToObject`,
`createCache`, `createMemoryStore`, `createTranslator`, `negotiateLocale`, `localePath`,
`parseAcceptLanguage`.

## SSR — `@ramonyx/ssr`

```ts
createPageRoutes({
  pages, renderer, document?, client?, streaming?, hooks?, cache?,
  assets?, i18n?, errorDetails?, maxDocumentBytes?,
}): RouteEntry[]
```

- `client: { script, extraModules? }` enables hydration.
- `i18n: { locales, defaultLocale, prefixDefaultLocale?, directions? }` enables locale routing.
- `document` overrides the HTML shell (`DocumentOptions` includes `title, body, head, scripts,
  status, lang, dir`).

Also: `defaultDocument`, `RAMONYX_MOUNT_ID`, and SEO helpers `sitemapXml`, `robotsTxt`,
`createSeoRoutes`.

## React — `@ramonyx/react`

- `createReactRenderer()` — SSR + streaming renderer.
- `Image` (`@ramonyx/react/assets`) — safe defaults + `<picture>` when variants exist.
- `Link` (`@ramonyx/react/link`) — client navigation + prefetch.
- Types: `PageProps<Data, Params>`, `LayoutProps`, `ErrorPageProps`.

## Compiler — `@ramonyx/compiler`

- `createRouteManifest({ dir, importer? })` — API routes.
- `loadPageRoutes({ dir, apiDir?, importer? })` — page manifest.
- `generateClientEntry(pages, { from })`, `generateServerEntry(options)`,
  `generateRouteTypes(pages)`.
- Loader: `import "@ramonyx/compiler/register"` (TypeScript + JSX for app code).

## Bundler — `@ramonyx/bundler`

- `buildClient(options)`, `buildEdge(options)`, `prerenderRoutes(options)`.
- `readClientScript(clientDir)`, `createAssetResolver(clientDir, { fallbackToPath? })`,
  `assetUrl(manifest, path)`, `readAssetManifest`, `fontPreloadTag`.
- `definePlugin`, `loadPlugins`, `createDevServer`.

## Security — `@ramonyx/security`

`securityHeaders()`, `cspNonce()`, `csrfProtection()`, `rateLimit()`, `parseCookies()`,
`serializeCookie()`, `signValue()`, `verifyValue()`, `createSession()`. The SSRF-guarded fetch is a
Node-only subpath: `import { guardedFetch } from "@ramonyx/security/ssrf"`.

## Adapter runtime — `@ramonyx/adapter-runtime`

`createNodeHost()` (`serve`, `env`), `serveStatic({ dir, prefix, immutable?, headers? })`, and the
in-memory host used by tests. `cacheControl({ maxAge, sMaxAge?, staleWhileRevalidate?, immutable?,
private? })` lives in `@ramonyx/core` (re-exported by `ramonyx`).

## Testing — `@ramonyx/testing`

`createTestServer(options)` / `createTestServerFromHandler(handler)` — in-process requests without
binding a port.

## CLI — `@ramonyx/devtools`

`ramonyx dev | build | start | doctor | version | help`. Build flags: `--static`, `--target edge`,
`--watch`. Dev prints a devtools panel URL (`/__ramonyx/devtools`).

## Diagnostics

Framework errors carry stable `RMX-*` codes. In development, error pages include the stack and
source file; production pages never do.

## docs/public/api/versioning.md

# API Versioning & Stability

Ramonyx follows semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) for every published package:
`ramonyx`, `@ramonyx/*`, and `create-ramonyx-app`.

## Public surface

The public API is the set of value/type exports declared by each package's `exports` map and
root `src/index.ts`. Subpaths are part of the surface too (`@ramonyx/react/client`,
`@ramonyx/react/islands`, `@ramonyx/security/ssrf`, and so on).

Internal modules, generated `dist/` files, and internal documentation are not public APIs.

## Compatibility policy

- **PATCH**: bug fixes and documentation/typing corrections with no intentional behavior break.
- **MINOR**: additive features, new exports, and opt-in behavior. Existing exports keep working.
- **MAJOR**: breaking changes, including removal/rename of exports or changed defaults.

At least one minor release must warn about a planned removal before the major release removes it.
Deprecated APIs are documented in the changelog and, where practical, emit a runtime warning.
Migration notes and an upgrade path are required for every major release.

## Contract enforcement

`tests/package-exports.test.ts` locks the contract values for the public packages. The generated
`docs/public/machine/api.json` records exports and types for each package. Additive changes must
update both; removing or renaming a public export is a deliberate major-release decision.

## Runtime Rust

The Rust/V8 runtime is a separate experimental track. Its packages/binaries are not part of the
Node framework's 1.0 compatibility promise until its own exit criteria promote it explicitly.

## docs/public/architecture.md

# Architecture

Ramonyx is a Node.js-first framework with an experimental Rust/V8 runtime. This page describes the
public architecture: how a request flows, what the packages do, and where the boundaries are.

## Request lifecycle

```
Request
  → runtime host (Node adapter)
  → server: body/timeout/concurrency gates
  → global middleware (security headers, CSP nonce, rate limit, logging)
  → router (API routes + page routes, 404/405)
  → folder middleware (root → deepest)
  → loader (GET) / action (POST)
  → render (React: sync or stream)
  → hydration payload + HTML document
Response
```

## Layers

| Layer | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| **Framework** | routing, SSR, server actions, data loading, client navigation, security defaults |
| **Compiler/bundler** | route manifest, codegen (client entry, typed routes, edge entry), Vite builds |
| **Runtime** | Node.js (baseline) or the experimental Rust/V8 host |
| **System** | OS, TCP/TLS, filesystem, process |

## Packages

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `ramonyx` | meta package re-exporting common primitives |
| `@ramonyx/core` | request lifecycle, context, middleware, errors, cache, i18n, assets types |
| `@ramonyx/router` | route matching, params, 404/405 |
| `@ramonyx/server` | HTTP wiring, limits, rate limit, observability |
| `@ramonyx/schema` | Standard Schema validation + error mapping |
| `@ramonyx/adapter-runtime` | runtime contract, Node + in-memory hosts, static serving, Redis adapter |
| `@ramonyx/ssr` | page rendering, streaming, SEO helpers, locale routing |
| `@ramonyx/react` | React renderer, `Image`, `Link` |
| `@ramonyx/compiler` | page/API manifests, codegen, dev loader |
| `@ramonyx/bundler` | Vite builds, dev server, assets, plugins |
| `@ramonyx/security` | headers/CSP/CSRF, shared rate limits, sessions/user store, OAuth, authorization, SSRF |
| `@ramonyx/testing` | in-memory test server |
| `@ramonyx/devtools` | the `ramonyx` CLI, plugin registry installer, benchmarks workflow support |
| `@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server` | MCP docs server over stdio/HTTP for agents |
| `@ramonyx/plugin-image` | build-time image variants (optional `sharp`) |

## Server ↔ client boundary

- Page/layout modules are isomorphic; loaders and actions are server-only.
- `*.server.ts` modules are stubbed with a poison pill in the client bundle.
- The build rejects `node:*` imports in client modules and scans the output for leaks.
- Secrets belong in `*.server.ts` or server-only loaders; only UI data goes into the hydration
  payload (JSON-serializable).

## Runtime contract

`@ramonyx/core` defines the web-standard boundary used by every host:

```ts
export type FetchHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;

export interface RuntimeHost {
  readonly name: string;                    // "node" | "memory" | "ramonyx"
  serve(handler: FetchHandler, options: { port: number; host?: string }): Promise<RunningServer>;
  readonly env: { get(name: string): string | undefined };
}
```

The Node adapter and the in-memory test host implement it; the experimental Rust/V8 runtime targets
the same contract (compatibility suite). The framework does not depend on runtime internals.

## Rendering & deployment targets

- **Node**: SSR + hydration + soft navigation; streaming opt-in.
- **Static**: prerendered pages + assets (`ramonyx build --static`).
- **Edge**: a single `{ fetch }` artifact with statically imported routes and an inlined asset map
  (CI exercises it in workerd).

See [Routing](routing.md), [SSR & Hydration](ssr-hydration.md), and [Deployment](deployment.md).

## docs/public/assets-and-images.md

# Assets & Images

Files in `src/assets/**` are hashed at build time, recorded in a manifest, and resolved through the
server-side asset resolver. Node cannot `import photo.png`, so the resolver is the contract between
SSR and the client bundle.

## Add an asset

```
src/assets/
  logo.svg
  img/hero.png
  fonts/inter.woff2
```

Wire the resolver once in `src/app.ts`:

```ts
import { createAssetResolver } from "@ramonyx/bundler";

const assets = await createAssetResolver(clientDir, { fallbackToPath: true });

createPageRoutes({ pages, renderer, assets /* ... */ });
```

Loaders receive `assets`:

```ts
export async function loader({ assets }) {
  return {
    logo: assets.url("logo.svg"),        // "/assets/logo-3f9a1c2b7d.svg"
    hero: assets.image("img/hero.png"),  // { src, width, height, srcSet?, sources? }
  };
}
```

## Rendering images

`Image` from `@ramonyx/react/assets` supplies safe defaults: explicit dimensions (no layout shift),
`loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, and an optional `<picture>` when responsive variants exist.

```tsx
import { Image } from "@ramonyx/react/assets";

<Image {...data.hero} alt="Hero" sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 640px" />;
```

With the image plugin enabled, `assets.image()` returns `srcSet` and `<source>` entries, so the
markup renders:

```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="/assets/img/hero-320-….webp 320w, …" sizes="…" />
  <img src="/assets/img/hero-….png" width="800" height="600" srcset="…" … />
</picture>
```

## Responsive images (build-time variants)

```bash
pnpm add @ramonyx/plugin-image sharp
```

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
import { imageOptimizer } from "@ramonyx/plugin-image";
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [imageOptimizer({ widths: [320, 640, 960, 1280], formats: ["webp"] })],
});
```

- Variants are generated at build time (resize + WebP; AVIF is opt-in because it is slower).
- `sharp` is an **optional peer** — installed by the app, not by the framework.
- Results are cached by content hash in `.ramonyx/image-cache`; unchanged images are not re-encoded.
- The original file is always copied and used as the universal fallback.
- Colors/dimensions are recorded in `ramonyx.assets.json` (`width`, `height`, `placeholder`, `variants`).
- A tiny blurred WebP data URI is generated by default and passed through `assets.image()` as
  `placeholder`; `Image` uses it as a CSS background until the real image paints (anti-CLS).
  Disable with `imageOptimizer({ placeholder: false })`.

`avif` can be added to `formats` for smaller files at the cost of build time. SVG is passed through
(vector assets do not need variants).

## Fonts

Fonts are hashed like any asset. Preload a font by putting a `<link rel="preload">` tag in page
metadata:

```ts
import { fontPreloadTag } from "@ramonyx/bundler";

export const metadata = {
  title: "Home",
  head: fontPreloadTag("/assets/fonts/inter-6a1b2c3d.woff2"),
};
```

## Honest limitations

- Development serves `src/assets/**` as-is (no hashes/variants); build output is the source of
  truth for production behavior. Dev and production use the same path spelling.
- Image optimization only runs for raster formats (PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF/TIFF); SVG is passed through.
- Blur placeholders are generated at build time; on-demand dev variants are not generated.
- AVIF is opt-in and slower; enable it only when the bandwidth win justifies build cost.


## Static serving

`serveStatic()` supports `Range: bytes=…` (`206`, suffix/open-ended ranges, `416` for
unsatisfiable), ETag/304, and precompressed `.br`/`.gz` siblings selected from
`Accept-Encoding` with a `Vary: accept-encoding` header. Range requests use the identity file;
precompressed files must be generated by your build/deploy pipeline.

## docs/public/benchmarks.md

# Benchmarks

Performance claims need measurements you can run. The benchmark protocol is fixed: warm up, repeat,
report the distribution (median, spread) — never a single run, never an average hiding a tail.

## What is measured

| Benchmark | Metric | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP | requests/s, p50/p95/p99 | autocannon against the playground |
| SSR | render time, TTFB, output size | synchronous vs streaming, in-process |
| Security | status/error counts, RSS under abuse/soak | 6 abuse scenarios + sustained load |
| Startup | wall/startup/load/eval | Rust runtime CLI, median of N runs |
| Web Vitals | LCP, CLS, FCP, TTFB | Playwright on the production build |
| Image pipeline | before/after LCP/CLS with variants | throttled CDP + cold loads |

## Commands

```bash
pnpm bench                 # HTTP baseline (warm-up 3s + 5 runs, median/spread)
pnpm bench:report          # compare against baseline (report-only, tolerance 25%)
pnpm bench:ssr             # SSR sync vs streaming
pnpm bench:ssr:report      # comparison artifact
pnpm bench:security        # abuse cases + soak (RSS from /proc)
pnpm bench:image           # image pipeline before/after (playground)
benchmarks/runtime-startup.sh   # Rust runtime startup (needs a release build)
```

Results are written under `benchmarks/results/`. Web Vitals are measured by the e2e suite and
compared report-only against the committed baseline.

## Baselines are per environment

A baseline is only meaningful on the machine that produced it. Baselines are stored per
(platform × arch × Node major × CPU), and the strict comparison **refuses to compare across
environments** — it prints the mismatching fields instead of pretending.

- Development baselines are committed for the maintainer machine.
- GitHub-hosted CI runs benchmarks **report-only**: runners vary too much for a blocking gate.
- The dedicated `.github/workflows/bench-strict.yml` workflow runs `pnpm bench:gate` on a
  self-hosted runner labeled `ramonyx-bench`. It blocks only on that matching environment and waits
  for the runner when it is offline; normal PRs keep the report-only fallback in `ci.yml`.
- `VITALS_STRICT=1` turns the Web Vitals comparison into a gate; use it only on a stable runner.

## Refresh procedure (strict runner)

1. Run `pnpm bench` and `pnpm bench:ssr` on the self-hosted runner with the app idle.
2. Inspect the median/spread; commit the per-environment baseline files under
   `benchmarks/results/baselines/`.
3. Run `pnpm bench:gate` on the same runner to confirm the new baseline passes.
4. Keep the report-only artifacts from `ci.yml`; never copy a baseline between machines or CPU
   models (the guard rejects it).

## Rules

- Same hardware/OS/runtime/config for every comparison.
- Identical work per request; verify responses match.
- Report medians and spread; keep raw artifacts.
- No public performance claim without a runnable benchmark in the repo.

## docs/public/cli.md

# CLI Reference

The `ramonyx` CLI (from `@ramonyx/devtools`) runs the app: dev server, build, production start, and
diagnostics.

```bash
ramonyx dev              # Vite + HMR (default :5173) → SSR (port from config)
ramonyx build            # client bundle → dist/client (run before production start)
ramonyx build --static   # client bundle + prerender pages → dist/static
ramonyx build --target edge   # server/edge bundle → dist/edge ({ fetch } contract)
ramonyx build --watch    # rebuild on file changes (covers --static/--target)
ramonyx start            # production SSR (NODE_ENV=production)
ramonyx start --watch    # restart the server when src/** changes
ramonyx add <name> --registry <path|url>  # verified plugin install + lock
ramonyx remove <name>    # remove plugin + lock entry
ramonyx doctor           # config + routes + build diagnostics
ramonyx routes           # page + API route manifest
ramonyx check            # config, entry, routes, client/server boundaries
ramonyx ai init          # AGENTS.md + thin adapters + MCP config
ramonyx ai sync          # update the managed block/config without touching user prose
ramonyx version | help
```

`doctor`, `routes`, `check`, and `ai` accept `--json` for agents and CI. JSON output is stable and
does not include timestamps:

```bash
ramonyx routes --json
ramonyx check --json
ramonyx doctor --json
```

`check --json` returns diagnostics with a stable code and a troubleshooting link:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "ok": false,
  "appDir": "/app",
  "summary": { "errors": 1, "warnings": 0 },
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "RMX-BUILD-1",
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "Impor \"node:fs\" di modul klien tidak diizinkan (node-builtin). ...",
      "file": "src/routes/panel/page.tsx",
      "docs": "https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/docs/troubleshooting/#rmx-build-1"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Flags

| Flag | Applies to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app <dir>` | all | App directory (default: cwd) |
| `--config <path>` | all | Config path (default `<app>/ramonyx.config.ts`) |
| `--port <n>` | dev/start | Override the SSR port |
| `--dev-port <n>` | dev | Override the Vite port (default 5173) |
| `--static` | build | Prerender static routes (`getStaticPaths` for dynamic routes) → `dist/static` |
| `--target <name>` | build | Extra target; `edge` → `dist/edge` |
| `--watch` | build/start | Build: rebuild on changes (debounced, safe queue). Start: restart a supervised server process with clean shutdown. |
| `--registry <path\|url>` | add/remove | Plugin registry JSON (or `RAMONYX_PLUGIN_REGISTRY`) |
| `--public-key <path>` | add | Ed25519 public key PEM (or `RAMONYX_PLUGIN_PUBLIC_KEY`) |
| `--agents <list>` | ai | Adapters: `claude,cursor,copilot,opencode` (default: all) |
| `--no-mcp` | ai | Do not write MCP client configuration |
| `--force` | ai | Overwrite existing files, including `AGENTS.md` without a managed marker |
| `--dry-run` | ai | Report actions without writing |
| `--json` | doctor/routes/check/ai | Machine-readable output (stable schema, no timestamps) |

## Conventions

```
src/app.ts             export createApp(options?) → FetchHandler
src/server.ts          optional custom server entry (CLI still hosts it)
src/routes/            page.tsx / layout.tsx / error.tsx + api/*.ts
ramonyx.config.ts      default export { app?, server? } (optional)
```

- `ramonyx dev|start` prefers `src/server.ts` when present, otherwise `src/app.ts`.
- Plugins from `ramonyx.config.ts` are loaded by the CLI (Vite, middleware, hooks, assets).
- `ramonyx start` sets `NODE_ENV=production` if unset; reactivity/React production build depends on it.
- `start --watch` is a supervisor: the server runs in a child process so changed modules are not
  cached; SIGINT/SIGTERM stops both watcher and child. Rebuild the client separately when client
  sources change.
- `--static` and `--target edge` cannot be combined (different artifacts).

## Examples

```bash
# Local development with HMR
ramonyx dev --app examples/shop

# Production build + start on port 8080
ramonyx build --app examples/shop
ramonyx start --app examples/shop --port 8080

# Static export and edge artifact
ramonyx build --static --app examples/shop
ramonyx build --target edge --app examples/shop
ramonyx build --watch --app examples/shop
```

## Doctor, routes, and check

`ramonyx doctor` prints the CLI/Node versions, resolved config, the resolved entry
(`src/server.ts` or `src/app.ts`), route counts, and whether `dist/client` has a manifest. Use it
before filing an issue or before an agent starts work.

`ramonyx routes` prints the page/API manifest: path, source file, loader/action flags, API methods,
and middleware. It does not open a server. `--json` is the agent-facing form.

`ramonyx check` validates config, the server entry, page/API route exports, and client/server
boundaries. It is intentionally static and does not replace `pnpm typecheck` or `ramonyx build`.
Exit code is `1` when an error diagnostic is present. Codes are the stable `RMX-*` codes documented
in [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## Agent setup

`ramonyx ai init` writes an `AGENTS.md` managed block from the project manifest and, optionally,
thin adapters for Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and OpenCode. It also writes project MCP
configs (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `opencode.json`) with the MCP package **pinned to the
project's `ramonyx` version** — never `@latest`.

```bash
ramonyx ai init
ramonyx ai init --agents claude,cursor --dry-run
ramonyx ai sync              # refresh the managed block + MCP command
ramonyx ai sync --json       # { schemaVersion, ok, mcp, files, warnings }
```

`AGENTS.md` is canonical; `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/ramonyx.mdc`,
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and `.opencode/skills/ramonyx/SKILL.md` are short pointers to it.
Files you already wrote are skipped unless `--force`; `--dry-run` writes nothing. Run
`ramonyx check --json` afterwards to verify the app itself.

## Devtools

`ramonyx dev` also prints the devtools panel URL (`/__ramonyx/devtools`). See
[Devtools Panel](devtools.md).

## docs/public/data-and-caching.md

# Data & Caching

Ramonyx keeps data loading in the page module: a `loader` for reads, an `action` for writes, and an
opt-in cache for expensive work.

## Loaders

```ts
export const revalidate = 60;
export const cacheTags = ["catalog"];

export async function loader({ params }) {
  return { product: await db.products.find(params.id) };
}
```

Loader data is JSON-serializable and available to the component as `data` (and to the client via
the hydration payload).

### Request-scoped dependency graph

Every loader/action receives `load(key, fn)`. The graph is created per request, so the same
resource is computed once even when loader code calls it multiple times or nested services do:

```ts
export async function loader({ params, load }) {
  const [product, reviews] = await Promise.all([
    load(`produk:${params.id}`, () => db.products.find(params.id)),
    load(`ulasan:${params.id}`, () => db.reviews.forProduct(params.id)),
  ]);
  return { product, reviews };
}
```

Keys must be stable and deterministic; do not include secrets or user-specific values unless the
loader is request-scoped (it is — the graph is discarded after the response). The graph deduplicates
concurrent calls and keeps the promise for the duration of the request; failed dependencies are not
silently retried. A page still owns its loader — the graph is for shared/nested data, not a global
cross-request cache (use the cache/revalidate API for that).

## Cache semantics

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `revalidate: 60` | Cache loader data for 60 s; the next 60 s serves stale data and refreshes in the background |
| `cacheTags: ["catalog"]` | Tag the entry so `revalidate({ tags: ["catalog"] })` removes it |
| no `revalidate` | No caching — loader runs on every request |

Session safety: requests with **cookies** or a **query string** bypass the cache. That keeps
per-user responses out of a shared cache by construction.

The default cache is in-memory (single process). The store interface (`KeyValueStore`) is pluggable
— implement `get/set/delete/invalidateTags` for Redis or another backend and pass it to
`createCache({ store })`. The contract has a shared test suite in the repo. See
[State & Adapters](state-and-adapters.md) for TTL, atomic operations, and failure-mode guidance.

## On-demand invalidation

```ts
// from an action
await revalidate({ tags: ["catalog"] });
```

```ts
// from anywhere with the cache instance
import { createCache } from "ramonyx";
const cache = createCache();
await cache.revalidate({ paths: ["/products"], tags: ["catalog"] });
```

Invalidation also fires the `onInvalidate` app hook, so observability and plugins can react.

## Server actions

Actions are POST handlers colocated with the page:

```ts
export const actionSchema = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1,
    vendor: "app",
    validate: (form) => {
      const name = String((form as Record<string, unknown>)?.name ?? "").trim();
      return name.length > 0
        ? { value: { name } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "Name is required", path: ["name"] }] };
    },
  },
};

export async function action({ formData, revalidate }) {
  const name = String(formData.get("name"));
  await db.customers.create({ name });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["customers"] });
  return { message: `Created ${name}` };
}
```

`actionSchema` validates the form data before the action runs (invalid → `400` + field errors). The
page renders the last action result as `action` (`{ ok, errors?, message?, data? }`). Redirects use
`303` so a refresh does not resubmit.

## Pragmatic notes

- The cache key includes the page path, route params, and (with i18n) the active locale.
- Cached values are process-local; for multi-instance deployments use an external store.
- There is no HTML page cache (CSP nonces make HTML per-request); only **loader data** is cached.
- A CDN can cache the HTML of static/prerendered pages separately.

## docs/public/deployment.md

# Deployment

One app, three targets. The same `src/app.ts` runs on Node, as static files, or as an edge
`fetch` handler.

## Node (default)

```bash
ramonyx build        # client bundle → dist/client (hashed assets + manifest)
ramonyx start        # SSR on the configured port; NODE_ENV=production
```

Set the port/host in `ramonyx.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";
export default defineConfig({ server: { port: 3000, host: "0.0.0.0" } });
```

Production notes:

- Serve `dist/client/assets/**` with `immutable` cache headers (the CLI's `start` does this for you).
- The Node adapter compresses responses with brotli/gzip and appends per-chunk for streaming.
- Keep the process behind a reverse proxy for TLS; the runtime verifies TLS for outbound `fetch`.
- Defaults: body 1 MiB, timeout 10 s, concurrency 100. Tune via `createHandler` options.

## Static

```bash
ramonyx build --static     # → dist/static
```

- Static routes are prerendered; dynamic routes need `getStaticPaths`.
- A page with `metadata.status = 404` becomes `404.html`.
- Assets are copied alongside the HTML.
- Deploy the directory to any static host (GitHub Pages, S3, Netlify, …).

## Edge / serverless

```bash
ramonyx build --target edge   # → dist/edge/index.js
ramonyx build --target vercel # → dist/vercel (api/index.js + vercel.json)
ramonyx build --target deno   # → dist/deno (main.ts + index.js)
```

The artifact exports `{ fetch }` — the standard edge contract:

```js
export const fetch = (request, env) => handler(request);
export default { fetch };
```

- Pages, API routes, actions, middleware, and the asset map are inlined into one bundle.
- Platform bindings (KV, secrets) are forwarded per request: the entry receives `env` and exposes
  it to loaders/actions as `env.get(name)` / `env.getRaw(name)`.
- The build rejects `node:*` imports in the edge artifact (except where shimmed by the platform).
- CI runs a **workerd** smoke test against the edge artifact (Cloudflare's runtime), so SSR, API,
  actions, env bindings, middleware, and 404s are exercised in a real edge runtime.

## Preview and staging

- Local preview: `pnpm docs` (and `pnpm dev` for the playground).
- Worker preview: run `pnpm build:worker` then `pnpm dlx wrangler deploy`, or trigger
  `deploy-worker.yml` manually. The canonical domain is `https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/`; the
  GitHub Pages mirror is published at `/ramonyx`.
- **Automatic PR previews are intentionally not enabled.** Cloudflare credentials are limited to
  trusted `main`/manual workflows so pull requests (especially forks) never receive deployment
  secrets. A PR is previewed locally or via an explicitly authorized manual deploy.

## Environment variables

| Context | Access |
| --- | --- |
| Node | `env.get("NAME")` (process env by default) |
| Edge | per-request `env` bindings forwarded by the platform adapter |
| Client | never — server values stay server-side |

## Headers & security in production

- `securityHeaders()` + `cspNonce()` from `@ramonyx/security` set CSP (with per-request nonce),
  `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`.
- HSTS/TLS termination belongs to your proxy or platform.
- Rate limiting and load shedding are in-process by default; use an external store for
  multi-instance deployments.

## docs/public/devtools.md

# Devtools Panel

Every `ramonyx dev` session exposes a dev-only panel with routes, request/loader/render timings,
hydration status, and bundle sizes. It is never enabled in production builds.

```bash
ramonyx dev
# dev: http://localhost:5173 (Vite + HMR) → SSR http://127.0.0.1:3000
# devtools: http://localhost:5173/__ramonyx/devtools
```

## What it shows

| Section | Data source | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Routes** | Page + API manifest | Shows `page`/`api` kind and API methods; updated when route files change |
| **Bundles & assets** | `dist/client/ramonyx.assets.json` + file sizes | Empty until the app has been built — the panel does not build for you |
| **Recent requests** | Collector middleware + `AppHooks` | Last 50 requests; method, path, status, total, loader, render, cache, hydration |

**Hydration** is detected from the response HTML: `payload` when
`<script id="ramonyx-payload">` is present, `none` for HTML without it (e.g. error pages).

## How it works

- The dev server creates a collector backed by the app's `AppHooks` (`onLoaderEnd`, `onRenderEnd`)
  and a middleware placed outermost in the chain.
- `GET /__ramonyx/devtools` serves the panel (a self-contained HTML page polling every 2s);
  `GET /__ramonyx/data` returns `{ routes, assets, requests }` as JSON.
- Both endpoints are served by the dev server, not proxied to the SSR app, and are absent from
  production.

## Limitations (honest)

- Loader/render correlation uses Node `AsyncLocalStorage`, so concurrent requests with the same
  path do not overwrite each other's timings.
- Requests short-circuited by plugin middleware are still recorded (the collector is outermost), but
  Vite asset requests and `/__ramonyx/*` calls are not.
- Not a production observability tool — use [Observability](observability.md) for that.

## docs/public/for-agents.md

# For Agents

Agents get a machine-readable view of Ramonyx that is generated from **public** documentation only:

- [`llms.txt`](https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/machine/llms.txt) — index of the public docs and
  machine files.
- [`llms-full.txt`](https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/machine/llms-full.txt) — the same content in
  one file.
- `machine/features.json` — feature status, packages, evidence, and honest limitations.
- `machine/rules.json` — rules for writing apps with good/bad examples.
- `machine/adrs.json` — public decision summaries (one-line decisions + relations).
- `machine/stats.json` — the single source of truth for numbers (version, packages, tests).
- `machine/api.json`, `machine/cli.json`, `machine/config.schema.json` — extracted API/CLI/config
  references.
- `machine/recipes.json` — task recipes with stable ids, affected files, and verification commands;
  the full guides live in `recipes/` (start at [Recipes](recipes/index.md)).
- `ramonyx routes --json` / `ramonyx check --json` / `ramonyx doctor --json` — project map and
  stable diagnostics (`RMX-*` codes + troubleshooting links) from the CLI.

## Context7

- Library listing: [ramonyx_devmoon_net](https://context7.com/websites/ramonyx_devmoon_net)
- Search endpoint: `https://context7.com/api/v2/ask?siteKey=ask_89339fd8bad939f239a589fa&query=<URL-encoded question>`
  — returns documentation with source links; no API key required.

## MCP server (stdio)

The docs are also available as an MCP server. The docs-only baseline has five tools —
`search_docs`, `get_page`, `get_feature_status`, `get_rules`, `list_adrs`. Add `--app <dir>` for
project mode, which adds `get_project_context`, `list_routes`, `get_route`, `get_recipe`, and
`search_api`:

Run `ramonyx ai init` to write these configs with the package pinned to your project's `ramonyx`
version. The examples use `1.0.0`; substitute your installed version (never `@latest`).

```bash
# Claude Code (project-aware)
claude mcp add ramonyx-docs -- npx -y @ramonyx/mcp-docs-server@1.0.0 --app .
```

```json
// Cursor: .cursor/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ramonyx-docs": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server@1.0.0", "--app", "."]
    }
  }
}
```

```json
// OpenCode: opencode.json
{
  "mcp": {
    "ramonyx-docs": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server@1.0.0", "--app", "."],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

The server ships a **snapshot of the public docs** at release time, so it works without cloning the
repo. Inside the repository you can point it at the working tree:

```bash
node --import ./tools/register.mjs packages/mcp-docs-server/src/cli.ts --docs docs/public --app .
```

Project mode is a **static scan**: it reads file names and exports, and does not execute your app.
Use `ramonyx routes --json` / `ramonyx check --json` when you need the validated route manifest or
diagnostics. Keep the MCP package pinned to the project's `ramonyx` version rather than `@latest`.

### HTTP transport

For hosted MCP clients, use the edge-safe HTTP handler (POST JSON-RPC):

```ts
import { createMcpHttpHandler } from "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server";

const mcp = createMcpHttpHandler({
  token: env.get("MCP_TOKEN"),                 // optional bearer auth
  rateLimit: { limit: 60, windowMs: 60_000 },  // in-memory; use gateway for multi-instance
  maxBodyBytes: 1_048_576,
});

// In a Node/edge handler:
const response = await mcp(request);
```

The handler returns `401` for a bad/missing bearer token, `429` with `Retry-After`, `405` for
non-POST, and `202` for notifications. Put it behind TLS and your own authentication when exposed
publicly; the built-in rate limit is per process and trusts `x-forwarded-for` only behind a
controlled proxy.

### Scaffolder opt-in

`pnpm create ramonyx-app <dir> --with-agent-docs` writes `AGENTS.md` and
`.opencode/skills/ramonyx/SKILL.md` in addition to the minimal app. Without the flag, the template
contains no agent-specific files. After scaffolding (or in any existing app), run
`ramonyx ai init` to regenerate the guide from the actual route map and write MCP configs.

## Ground rules for agents

1. **Facts over guesses.** Feature status comes from `features.json`; numbers from `stats.json`.
2. **Check the limitations field.** Features marked `partial`/`experimental` have documented gaps.
3. **Prefer the public contract.** If something is not in the public docs, do not assume it exists.
4. **Every claim needs evidence.** The machine layer links code/test/ADR paths; follow them.

## docs/public/getting-started.md

# Getting Started

Build a full-stack TypeScript app with file routing, SSR React, and secure defaults. Ramonyx runs
on **Node.js ≥ 24**; the Rust/V8 runtime is experimental.

```bash
pnpm create ramonyx-app my-app
cd my-app
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Vite (5173) → SSR (3000)
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The scaffold ships with a page, an API route, validation, actions,
security middleware, and hydration — all runnable.

## Project layout

```
src/app.ts             createApp() → fetch handler (API + pages + middleware)
src/server.ts          optional custom server entry (CLI still hosts it)
src/routes/            file routing
  page.tsx             route "/"
  layout.tsx           root layout
  [...slug]/page.tsx   404 page (metadata.status = 404)
  middleware.ts        per-folder middleware (root = every route)
  api/halo/[nama].ts   dynamic API route
ramonyx.config.ts      app/server options (optional)
```

## A page with a loader

`src/routes/page.tsx` is an isomorphic module: `loader` runs on the server, the component renders
on the server and then hydrates in the browser.

```tsx
import type { PageProps } from "@ramonyx/react";

export const metadata = { title: "Home", description: "My first app" };

export async function loader() {
  return { message: "Hello from the server" };
}

export default function Home({ data }: PageProps<{ message: string }>) {
  return <h1>{data.message}</h1>;
}
```

Loader data must be JSON-serializable (it is embedded in the hydration payload). For
filesystem/database access, use a `*.server.ts` module — the client bundle gets a poison-pill stub
instead of your secrets.

## An API route with validation

`src/routes/api/halo/[nama].ts`:

```ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";
import type { StandardSchema } from "@ramonyx/schema";

const params: StandardSchema<unknown, { nama: string }> = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1,
    vendor: "my-app",
    validate: (value) =>
      typeof (value as Record<string, unknown>)?.nama === "string"
        ? { value: { nama: (value as { nama: string }).nama } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "nama wajib", path: ["nama"] }] },
  },
};

export const GET = route<{ nama: string }>({
  params,
  handler: ({ params, json }) => json({ hello: params.nama }),
});
```

Invalid input returns `400` with `issues` before your handler runs.

## A form action

```tsx
export async function action({ formData }: { formData: FormData }) {
  const name = String(formData.get("name") ?? "").trim();
  if (name.length === 0) return { errors: { name: "Required" } };
  return { message: `Hello, ${name}!` };
}
```

The runtime re-renders the page with the action result, and the browser intercepts submission so
it works without a page reload — while still working with JavaScript disabled (progressive
enhancement, `POST` + `303` PRG).

## Build & deploy

```bash
ramonyx build             # client bundle → dist/client
ramonyx start             # production SSR (NODE_ENV=production)
ramonyx build --static    # prerender → dist/static (host anywhere)
ramonyx build --target edge   # dist/edge/index.js ({ fetch } contract)
```

See [Deployment](deployment.md) for details, and [Routing](routing.md) /
[SSR & Hydration](ssr-hydration.md) for the runtime model.

## docs/public/i18n.md

# Internationalization

Locale routing and translation helpers are built in — no module, no dependency. Enable routing,
translate in loaders/components, and let the framework handle `<html lang>`, `hreflang`, and
per-locale caching.

## Enable locale routing

```ts
// src/app.ts
createPageRoutes({
  pages,
  renderer: createReactRenderer(),
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "id"],
    defaultLocale: "en",
    // prefixDefaultLocale: true,     // every locale gets a prefix (incl. default)
    // directions: { ar: "rtl" },     // <html dir="rtl"> for specific locales
  },
});
```

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/about` | Served as the **default** locale (no prefix) |
| `/id/about` | Served as `id` |
| `/en` · `/en/about` | **308** → `/` · `/about` (when the default locale is unprefixed) |
| `prefixDefaultLocale: true` | The inverse: `/about` → 308 `/en/about` |

The framework also:

- sets `<html lang="…">` (and `dir` when configured);
- emits `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="…">` for every locale plus `x-default`;
- passes `locale` to loaders, actions, page props (`PageProps.locale`), and the hydration payload;
- **includes the locale in loader cache keys**, so revalidated pages cannot leak data across
  languages;
- leaves API routes untouched.

## Translating

Catalogs are plain nested objects (JSON-friendly). Load them where the data lives and pass them to
`createTranslator`:

```tsx
import { createTranslator, type Messages } from "ramonyx";

const catalog: Record<string, Messages> = {
  en: { hello: "Hello {name}!", items: { one: "{count} item", other: "{count} items" } },
  id: { hello: "Halo {name}!", items: { one: "{count} item", other: "{count} item" } },
};

export async function loader({ locale }: { locale?: string }) {
  const active = locale ?? "en";
  const { t, formatNumber, formatDate } = createTranslator({
    locale: active,
    messages: catalog[active] ?? {},
    fallbackMessages: catalog.en,        // optional
    // onMissing: (key) => console.warn("i18n:", key),
  });
  return {
    greeting: t("hello", { name: "Rina" }),
    count: t("items", { count: 3 }),      // plural via Intl.PluralRules
    price: formatNumber(1234.5),
    date: formatDate(new Date(), { dateStyle: "long" }),
  };
}
```

- **Interpolation**: `{name}` is replaced from the params object; unknown params stay as written.
- **ICU**: string messages support plural/selectordinal, select, number/percent/currency, and
  date/time (`{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}`). `formatMessage()` is exported for
  messages outside a catalog.
- **Plural objects**: object values (`one`/`other`/…) remain supported and use
  `Intl.PluralRules` with `params.count`.
- **Fallback**: missing key → `fallbackMessages` → `onMissing(key)` → the key itself.
- The helper is pure and edge-safe; it can also be used in middleware or client components.

The ICU implementation is a documented subset: no custom tag/style formatters, offsets, or
`{arg, spellout}`; malformed templates are returned unchanged instead of throwing.

## Language switcher

```tsx
import { localePath } from "ramonyx";

// From any page, build the same page in another locale (existing prefix is stripped).
<a href={localePath(currentPath, "id", { locales: ["en", "id"], defaultLocale: "en" })}>
  Bahasa Indonesia
</a>
```

## `Accept-Language` negotiation (middleware)

Use `localeDetection()` when you want automatic redirects. It checks the `locale` cookie first,
then `Accept-Language`, then the default; by default it only acts on `/` so cached pages and SEO
are not surprised. `strategy: "all"` extends it to other paths, and `/api`, `/assets`, `/_`, and
`/__ramonyx` are skipped.

```ts
import { localeDetection } from "ramonyx";

export const middleware = localeDetection({
  locales: ["en", "id"],
  defaultLocale: "en",
  // strategy: "all",
  // cookieName: "locale",
  // redirectStatus: 302,
});
```

If you need custom behavior, compose `negotiateLocale()` and `localePath()` manually; the helper
keeps detection explicit and configurable.

## Metadata and alternate links

Each locale route gets `<html lang>`/`dir`, locale-aware loader cache keys, and `<link
rel="alternate" hreflang>` entries for every configured locale plus `x-default` (see
`packages/ssr/test/i18n.test.ts`). Per-route metadata (title/description/canonical/OG) is read from
the page module; use the active `locale` in loader data/content and set a locale-specific canonical
where needed.

## Limitations (honest)

- ICU support is a subset: no custom tag/style formatters, offsets, or spellout.
- Catalogs are app-provided (JSON/data store) — the framework does not load files for you.
- One route per locale (linear in the number of locales); per-route localization is not supported.
- `hreflang` uses the page's logical path; dynamic routes follow the currently requested params.
- `localeDetection` is a redirect helper, not a CDN/Vary strategy; cache rules remain app-owned.

## docs/public/observability.md

# Observability

Three edge-safe primitives, built on the existing middleware + hook system (no dependency):

1. **Trace id** per request (`traceId()`) — propagated or generated, readable in loaders/actions.
2. **Structured request logs** (`requestLogging()`) — method, path, status, duration, trace id.
3. **Metrics** (`createMetrics()`) — counters/latencies from app hooks, exposed as JSON.

## Wiring

```ts
// src/app.ts
import { createMetrics, createMetricsRoute, requestLogging, traceId } from "@ramonyx/server";
import { mergeHooks } from "ramonyx";

const metrics = createMetrics();

const handler = createHandler({
  routes: [
    ...apiRoutes,
    createMetricsRoute(metrics),   // GET /metrics
    ...createPageRoutes({ pages, renderer, hooks: mergeHooks(appHooks, metrics.hooks) }),
  ],
  middleware: [traceId(), requestLogging()],
  hooks: mergeHooks(appHooks, metrics.hooks),
});
```

Order matters: `traceId()` must run before `requestLogging()` so the log line carries the id.

## Trace id

- Uses the incoming `x-request-id` header when present (proxy/client propagation), otherwise
  generates one (UUID, with a `getRandomValues` fallback).
- Rewrites the request with the header set, so loaders/actions can read it; sets the same header on
  the response.

```ts
// inside a loader
const id = request.headers.get("x-request-id");
```

Custom header name: `traceId({ header: "x-trace-id" })`.

## Structured logs

```ts
requestLogging();                    // message "request"
requestLogging({ message: "http" }); // custom message
```

`requestLogging()` emits one `info` line per request through the app logger:

```json
{"level":"info","message":"request","method":"GET","path":"/","status":200,"ms":12,"traceId":"…"}
```

Ship it to any collector (Fluent Bit, Vector, OTLP log exporter). Secrets/PII must not be logged —
the framework only emits method/path/status/duration/trace id.

## Metrics

`createMetrics()` returns `{ hooks, snapshot() }`:

```json
{
  "requests": { "total": 120, "byStatusClass": { "2xx": 118, "5xx": 2 },
                "durationMs": { "sum": 1840, "count": 120, "max": 210 } },
  "loaders": { "count": 80, "cached": 42, "durationMs": { "sum": 620, "max": 90 } },
  "renders": { "count": 118, "streaming": 110, "durationMs": { "sum": 980, "max": 140 } },
  "invalidations": 3
}
```

- `createMetricsRoute(metrics, { path: "/metrics" })` serves the snapshot as JSON.
- Schedule `metrics.snapshot()` exports to OTLP/Prometheus from your platform, or pull `/metrics`.
- Counters are cumulative since process start (per instance).
- Pass an `ObservabilitySink` to `createMetrics({ sink })` for JSON-lines or an OTel adapter; see
  [State & Adapters](state-and-adapters.md). A failing sink is isolated from requests.

## Notes & limitations

- `traceId` is a correlation id, not a full W3C `traceparent`; native OpenTelemetry spans are not
  built in (candidate if there is demand).
- Metrics are process-local: multi-instance deployments should scrape each instance or aggregate in
  your platform.
- The hooks are zero-cost when unused; the helpers are edge-safe (no `node:*`).

## docs/public/plugins.md

# Plugins

A plugin extends an app at build time (Vite), at request time (middleware), through app hooks
(observability/caching), and through the asset pipeline.

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
import { imageOptimizer } from "@ramonyx/plugin-image";
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";
import { analytics } from "./src/plugins/analytics.ts";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [analytics(), imageOptimizer()],
});
```

`ramonyx dev|build|start` loads plugins from the config. A custom server entry (`src/server.ts`)
still receives their hooks and is wrapped by their middleware — plugins are never duplicated.

## Writing a plugin

```ts
// src/plugins/analytics.ts
import { definePlugin } from "@ramonyx/bundler";
import type { Middleware } from "ramonyx";

const middleware: Middleware = async (context, next) => {
  const started = performance.now();
  const response = await next();
  console.log(context.request.method, new URL(context.request.url).pathname, response.status, Math.round(performance.now() - started));
  return response;
};

export const analytics = () =>
  definePlugin({
    name: "analytics",
    middleware: () => middleware,
    hooks: () => ({
      onLoaderEnd: (event) => {
        /* record loader timing */
      },
    }),
  });
```

| Hook | Runs | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vite` | build/dev | extra Vite plugins (CSS, fonts, aliases) |
| `middleware` | before routing | logging, headers, early blocking |
| `hooks` | request lifecycle | timing, metrics, invalidation |
| `assets` | build, per file | derived outputs (image variants) + dimensions |

`middleware` must be edge-safe (no `node:*`) if you deploy the edge artifact. Middleware runs
**before** application middleware, in plugin order.

## Asset hook

```ts
export const plugin = definePlugin({
  name: "thumbnails",
  async assets(_context, asset) {
    if (!asset.path.endsWith(".png")) return undefined;
    return {
      meta: { width: 800, height: 600 },
      outputs: [{ path: "img/hero-400.webp", data: encoded, width: 400, format: "webp" }],
    };
  },
});
```

Derived files are hashed automatically and recorded as `variants` in the manifest, so
`assets.image()` and `Image` can render them.

## Registry and `ramonyx add`

A registry is a JSON file (local path or HTTPS URL):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "ramonyx-plugin-analytics",
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "description": "Privacy-friendly analytics",
      "tarball": "https://registry.example/plugins/analytics-1.2.0.tgz",
      "integrity": "sha512-…",
      "signature": "base64-ed25519-signature"
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
ramonyx add ramonyx-plugin-analytics@1.2.0 --registry ./plugins.json
ramonyx add @scope/plugin --registry https://registry.example/index.json --public-key ./publisher.pem
ramonyx remove ramonyx-plugin-analytics
```

`add` downloads the tarball, verifies `sha512-…` integrity, optionally verifies an Ed25519
signature over `name@version\nintegrity`, then delegates to the app's package manager. On success it
atomically writes `plugins.lock.json`; if the lock write fails it rolls back the dependency. Add
the imported plugin to `ramonyx.config.ts` after installing; the lock records exactly what was
verified. `remove` removes the dependency and the lock entry.

- Signature-required entries without `--public-key` are rejected; a wrong signature never installs.
- Registry URLs and tarballs are network trust boundaries — pin HTTPS and publish immutable
  versions.
- Package managers still run install scripts for plugins you choose to install; review the tarball
  and use `ignore-scripts`/allowlists where your policy requires it.

## Publishing a plugin

Third-party plugins live in `node_modules`, where Node does **not** strip TypeScript. Ship compiled
JavaScript:

```json
{
  "name": "ramonyx-plugin-analytics",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "default": "./dist/index.js" } },
  "peerDependencies": { "@ramonyx/bundler": "^1.0.0", "ramonyx": "^1.0.0" },
  "engines": { "node": ">=24" }
}
```

- Use `peerDependencies` (not `dependencies`) so types/contracts follow the app's Ramonyx version.
- Heavy dependencies should be **optional peers** (`peerDependenciesMeta`) and imported lazily with
  a clear error — see how `@ramonyx/plugin-image` treats `sharp`.
- Test the hooks directly and in a real app (`ramonyx build|dev|start`).
- Contract stability: the plugin contract is **stable since 0.4.2**. Breaking changes follow
  semver (minor/major) with migration notes; additive optional hooks remain possible.

## Limitations (honest)

- The registry installer verifies artifacts and dependencies but does not sandbox plugin code; a
  plugin runs with the app's permissions.
- No per-route/per-loader plugin hooks (pre-routing middleware + app hooks only).
- Plugin order is config order; there is no explicit priority field.

Short, task-oriented guides for agents and humans. Each recipe has a stable id, the files it
touches, and a verification command; the machine-readable index is

| --- | --- | --- |

| Login/logout and protected pages | [Add session auth](auth-session.md) | `ramonyx check --json` |

```bash

```

MCP clients can call `get_recipe` (project mode) or `get_page` with these slugs. Prefer the public
docs over guessing; if a recipe does not fit, start from [Routing](../routing.md) and
