## docs/public/recipes/api-validation.md

---
recipe: api-validation
title: Add an API route with validation
summary: Export HTTP methods from src/routes/api, validate params/query/body at the trust boundary, and return stable errors.
when: A client or service needs JSON rather than HTML.
files: src/routes/api/users/[id].ts
verify: ramonyx check --json && ramonyx routes --json
---

# Add an API route with validation

```ts
// src/routes/api/users/[id].ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";

const idSchema = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1 as const,
    vendor: "app",
    validate: (input: unknown) => {
      const id = String((input as { id?: unknown })?.id ?? "");
      return /^[a-z0-9-]+$/.test(id)
        ? { value: { id } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "Invalid id", path: ["id"] }] };
    },
  },
};

export const GET = route({
  params: idSchema,
  handler: async ({ params, json }) => {
    const user = await db.users.find(params.id);
    return user === null ? json({ error: "Not found" }, 404) : json({ user });
  },
});

export const DELETE = route({
  params: idSchema,
  handler: async ({ params, text }) => {
    await db.users.delete(params.id);
    return text("", 204);
  },
});
```

- File path maps to URL: `api/users/[id].ts` → `/api/users/:id`.
- Exported `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` define allowed methods. Anything
  else returns `405` with `Allow`.
- `params`, `query`, and `body` accept Standard Schema; invalid input returns `400` with `issues`.
- Validate at the boundary, then trust the validated value inside the handler. Never interpolate
  raw input into SQL/shell/URLs.
- Use `json()`/`text()` helpers so status and headers are explicit.

## Verify

```bash
ramonyx routes --json   # methods + file for /api/users/[id]
ramonyx check --json
```

Next: [Routing](../routing.md), [Security](../security/) and [Sessions & Auth](../sessions-and-auth.md).

## docs/public/recipes/auth-session.md

---
recipe: auth-session
title: Add session auth
summary: Store sessions server-side, rotate the session on login, and protect a route with a guard.
when: You need login/logout and per-request user identity.
files: src/routes/login/page.tsx, src/routes/account/page.tsx, src/app.ts
verify: ramonyx check --json
---

# Add session auth

Ramonyx ships primitives; you own the account UI and email delivery. The examples below are a
minimal store-backed setup.

```ts
// src/lib/auth.server.ts
import { createKeyValueSessionStore, createSession, type KeyValueStore } from "@ramonyx/security";

export function sessionFor(store: KeyValueStore, secret: string) {
  return createSession({
    secret,
    store: createKeyValueSessionStore(store), // Redis/KV/DB in production
    cookie: { secure: true, sameSite: "lax", path: "/" },
  });
}
```

```ts
// src/routes/login/page.tsx
import { verifyPassword } from "@ramonyx/security";
import { sessionFor } from "../../lib/auth.server.ts";

export async function action({ request, env }: { request: Request; env: { get(k: string): string | undefined } }) {
  const form = await request.formData();
  const username = String(form.get("username") ?? "");
  const password = String(form.get("password") ?? "");
  const user = await db.users.findByUsername(username);
  const valid = user !== null && (await verifyPassword(password, user.passwordHash));
  if (!valid) {
    return { errors: { form: "Invalid username or password" }, status: 401 };
  }
  const session = sessionFor(store, env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!);
  const cookie = await session.rotate(request, { user: user.id }); // prevents fixation
  return { redirect: "/account", headers: { "set-cookie": cookie } };
}
```

Protect a page in its loader:

```ts
import { HttpError } from "ramonyx";
import { sessionFor } from "../../lib/auth.server.ts";

export async function loader({ request, env }: { request: Request; env: { get(k: string): string | undefined } }) {
  const session = sessionFor(store, env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!);
  const data = await session.read(request);
  if (data === null) {
    throw new HttpError(401, "Login required");
  }
  return { user: data.user };
}
```

Render a login link in `error.tsx` for `401`, or redirect in a middleware that reads the session
before calling `next()`. (Loaders cannot return a redirect; use `HttpError`/middleware.)

- Signed cookies are **not encrypted**; store only an opaque session id or non-secret data.
- Rotate on login, revoke on logout, and use the same generic error for unknown user and bad password.
- Add CSRF protection for state-changing forms (`csrfProtection()`), and rate-limit login/reset.
- In-memory stores are for development; use a shared store for multi-instance deployments.

Read [Sessions & Auth](../sessions-and-auth.md) and [State & Adapters](../state-and-adapters.md).

## docs/public/recipes/cache-revalidate.md

---
recipe: cache-revalidate
title: Cache loader data and invalidate it
summary: Opt into loader caching with revalidate/cacheTags, then invalidate by path or tag after a mutation.
when: A read-heavy page can tolerate a short stale window.
files: src/routes/products/page.tsx
verify: ramonyx check --json
---

# Cache loader data and invalidate it

```tsx title="src/routes/products/page.tsx"
export const revalidate = 60;               // seconds
export const cacheTags = ["products"];

export async function loader() {
  return { products: await db.products.list() };
}

export async function action({ formData, revalidate }: {
  formData: FormData;
  revalidate: (options: { tags?: string[] }) => Promise<void>;
}) {
  await db.products.create({ name: String(formData.get("name") ?? "") });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["products"] });
  return { message: "Created" };
}
```

- `revalidate` caches loader data for that many seconds and serves stale data while refreshing.
- Caching is skipped for requests with cookies or a query string.
- `cacheTags` lets you invalidate a group; `revalidate({ paths, tags })` also works from a loader,
  action, or the cache instance.
- Cached values are process-local by default. For multi-instance deployments, back the cache and
  session/rate-limit stores with Redis/KV.
- Do not combine loader caching with `defer()`; deferred data is for non-critical UI.

## Verify

Call the page twice and assert the loader count; invalidate a tag and assert the next request
re-reads. See [Testing](testing.md) and [Data & Caching](../data-and-caching.md).

## docs/public/recipes/deploy-static-edge.md

---
recipe: deploy-static-edge
title: Deploy static or edge output
summary: Prerender static routes or build a fetch-handler bundle, then deploy the generated directory.
when: You need a CDN/static host or an edge/serverless runtime instead of a Node process.
files: dist/static, dist/edge/index.js
verify: ramonyx build --static && ramonyx build --target edge
---

# Deploy static or edge output

## Static

```bash
ramonyx build --static
# → dist/static
```

- Every static page is prerendered; dynamic routes need `getStaticPaths`.
- A catch-all page with `metadata.status = 404` becomes `404.html`.
- Upload `dist/static` to GitHub Pages, S3, Netlify, or any static host.

## Edge / serverless

```bash
ramonyx build --target edge    # → dist/edge/index.js
ramonyx build --target vercel  # → dist/vercel
ramonyx build --target deno    # → dist/deno
```

The artifact exports the standard fetch contract:

```js
export const fetch = (request, env) => handler(request);
export default { fetch };
```

- Pages, API routes, actions, middleware, and the asset map are bundled together.
- Platform bindings arrive in `env` and are exposed as `env.get(name)`.
- `node:*` imports are rejected in the edge bundle (except platform shims). Move server-only code
  behind bindings or to a Node deployment.

## Verify

```bash
ramonyx check --json
ramonyx build --static
ramonyx build --target edge
# serve dist/static locally and request / and /404.html
```

Read [Deployment](../deployment.md) and [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) for target-specific
errors (`RMX-EDGE-1`, `RMX-BUILD-*`).

## docs/public/recipes/dynamic-route.md

---
recipe: dynamic-route
title: Add a dynamic route
summary: Map a URL segment or catch-all to a page, read params in the loader, and validate them.
when: The URL contains an identifier, slug, or nested path.
files: src/routes/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
verify: ramonyx routes --json && ramonyx check --json
---

# Add a dynamic route

Use `[param]` for one segment and `[...param]` for a catch-all:

```
src/routes/blog/[slug]/page.tsx   → /blog/:slug
src/routes/docs/[...path]/page.tsx → /docs/*path
```

```tsx title="src/routes/blog/[slug]/page.tsx"
import { HttpError, type PageLoaderContext } from "ramonyx";
import type { PageProps } from "@ramonyx/react";

export async function loader({ params }: PageLoaderContext<{ slug: string }>) {
  const post = await findPost(params.slug);
  if (post === null) {
    throw new HttpError(404, "Post not found");
  }
  return { post };
}

export default function Post({ data }: PageProps<{ post: { title: string; body: string } }>) {
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{data.post.title}</h1>
      <p>{data.post.body}</p>
    </article>
  );
}
```

- Params are strings; validate/normalize them before using them in queries.
- For static export, export `getStaticPaths()` with every allowed param object.
- Route groups `(marketing)` do not appear in the URL. Keep folder names that start with `_` for
  private files.

## Verify

```bash
ramonyx routes --json   # check the generated path, e.g. /blog/[slug]
ramonyx check --json
```

Next: [Routing](../routing.md) and [Typed Routes](../typed-routes.md).

## docs/public/recipes/form-action.md

---
recipe: form-action
title: Handle a form with a server action
summary: Validate FormData, mutate on the server, redirect or return a result, and keep no-JS submission working.
when: A page needs a mutation without a separate JSON API endpoint.
files: src/routes/notes/page.tsx
verify: ramonyx check --json && ramonyx dev
---

# Handle a form with a server action

```tsx title="src/routes/notes/page.tsx"
import type { PageActionContext } from "ramonyx";
import type { PageProps } from "@ramonyx/react";

export const actionSchema = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1 as const,
    vendor: "app",
    validate: (input: unknown) => {
      const name = String((input as Record<string, unknown>)?.text ?? "").trim();
      return name.length > 0
        ? { value: { text: name } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "Text is required", path: ["text"] }] };
    },
  },
};

export async function action({ formData, revalidate }: PageActionContext) {
  const text = String(formData.get("text") ?? "").trim();
  await db.notes.create({ text });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["notes"] });
  return { message: "Saved" };
}

export default function Notes({ data, action }: PageProps<{ notes: { id: string; text: string }[] }>) {
  return (
    <main>
      <form method="post">
        <input name="text" aria-label="Note text" />
        <button type="submit">Save</button>
      </form>
      {action?.message ? <p role="status">{action.message}</p> : null}
      <ul>{data.notes.map((note) => <li key={note.id}>{note.text}</li>)}</ul>
    </main>
  );
}
```

- The action POSTs to the same path; successful mutation re-renders the page with `action` result.
- Return `{ redirect: "/notes" }` for PRG (`303`) or `{ errors, status }` on failure.
- `actionSchema` runs before the action and returns `400` with field issues on invalid input.
- Without JavaScript the browser submits normally; with JavaScript the client intercepts it.
- Invalidate related loader data with `context.revalidate()` or `actionRevalidate`.

## Verify

```bash
ramonyx check --json
ramonyx dev
```

Submit the form with JavaScript disabled and enabled. Read [SSR & Hydration](../ssr-hydration.md)
and [Data & Caching](../data-and-caching.md).

## docs/public/recipes/page-loader.md

---
recipe: page-loader
title: Add a page with a loader
summary: Create a server-rendered page whose data is loaded on each request and embedded in the hydration payload.
when: The page needs request-time data from a database, API, or environment.
files: src/routes/page.tsx
verify: ramonyx check --json && ramonyx routes --json
---

# Add a page with a loader

Create `src/routes/page.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/routes/page.tsx"
import type { PageLoaderContext } from "ramonyx";
import type { PageProps } from "@ramonyx/react";

export async function loader({ request, env }: PageLoaderContext) {
  const greeting = env.get("GREETING") ?? "Hello";
  return { greeting, url: new URL(request.url).pathname };
}

export default function Home({ data }: PageProps<{ greeting: string; url: string }>) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{data.greeting}</h1>
      <p>Rendered for {data.url}</p>
    </main>
  );
}
```

- `loader` runs on the server for GET requests. Its return value must be JSON-serializable.
- Import server-only code from `*.server.ts`; never import `node:*` from a page component.
- Use `metadata` for the title and `HttpError(404, "…")` for missing data.

## Verify

```bash
ramonyx routes --json   # the page appears with "loader": true
ramonyx check --json    # config, entry, routes, client/server boundaries
ramonyx dev             # request the page in a browser
```

Next: [Routing](../routing.md) and [SSR & Hydration](../ssr-hydration.md).

## docs/public/recipes/testing.md

---
recipe: testing
title: Test a route in-process
summary: Exercise the real handler with an in-memory host, assert SSR/API behavior, then add a browser check.
when: You changed routes, loaders, actions, validation, or security limits.
files: test/home.test.ts
verify: pnpm test
---

# Test a route in-process

`@ramonyx/testing` runs your `FetchHandler` without ports or a browser:

```ts
// test/home.test.ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { createTestServerFromHandler } from "@ramonyx/testing";
import { createApp } from "../src/app.ts";

test("GET / renders SSR", async () => {
  const server = await createTestServerFromHandler(await createApp());
  try {
    const response = await server.fetch("/");
    assert.equal(response.status, 200);
    assert.match(await response.text(), /Hello/);
  } finally {
    await server.close(); // always close: a leaked listener hangs node --test
  }
});

test("POST /api/users rejects invalid body", async () => {
  const server = await createTestServerFromHandler(await createApp());
  try {
    const response = await server.fetch("/api/users", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: "" }),
    });
    assert.equal(response.status, 400);
    const body = (await response.json()) as { issues: unknown[] };
    assert.ok(body.issues.length > 0);
  } finally {
    await server.close();
  }
});
```

What to cover:

- Routing: `200`, `404`, `405` + `Allow`.
- Validation: invalid params/query/body → `400` with `issues`.
- Actions: rendered result, errors, redirect (`303`), and no-JS form submission.
- Cache: loader call counts and invalidation.
- Limits/security: `413`, `503`, `Retry-After`, CSRF.

Browser-level checks (hydration, soft navigation) belong in Playwright. Run `pnpm test` and
`ramonyx check --json` before handing work off. See [Testing](../testing.md).

## docs/public/routing.md

# Routing

Ramonyx maps files under `src/routes/` to URLs. No route config file, no decorators.

```
src/routes/
  page.tsx                 /
  layout.tsx               root layout (wraps every page)
  error.tsx                error boundary for this folder
  [...slug]/page.tsx       catch-all (404 in the template)
  users/
    page.tsx               /users
    [id]/page.tsx          /users/:id
  (marketing)/about/page.tsx   /about        ← route group: parentheses are not in the URL
  api/
    hello.ts               /api/hello
    users/[id].ts          /api/users/:id
```

## Pages

A page module exports:

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | React component receiving `PageProps` |
| `loader` | server-only data loading (GET) |
| `action` | form mutation handler (POST to the same path) |
| `metadata` | title/description/status/robots/canonical/head |
| `revalidate` | cache TTL in seconds (ISR-lite) |
| `cacheTags` | tags for on-demand invalidation |
| `prerender` / `getStaticPaths` | static generation control |

Dynamic segments use `[param]`; catch-all segments use `[...param]`. Route groups `(name)` organize
files without changing URLs. A folder-level `layout.tsx` wraps pages below it; `error.tsx` renders
when a loader/action/render throws an `HttpError` (or any error), with the status preserved.

## Loaders

```ts
export async function loader({ params, query, request, env, log }) {
  const user = await db.user.find(params.id);
  if (user === null) throw new HttpError(404, "User not found");
  return { user };
}
```

The loader context also exposes `assets` (asset resolver) and `locale` (when i18n routing is
enabled). Loader data is embedded in the hydration payload — keep it JSON-serializable.

## API routes

```ts
// src/routes/api/hello/[nama].ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";

export const GET = route<{ nama: string }>({
  handler: ({ params, json }) => json({ hello: params.nama }),
});

export const POST = route({
  handler: async ({ request }) => Response.json({ received: await request.text() }),
});
```

Exported `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` become allowed methods; others return `405` with an
`Allow` header. Query/params/body can be validated with a Standard Schema; invalid input → `400`
with `issues`.

## Middleware

- `src/routes/middleware.ts` runs before every route in that folder (root = every route), in
  root → deepest order. It is edge-safe: no `node:*` imports.
- Application-wide middleware (static files, logging, security headers) is passed to
  `createHandler({ middleware })` in `src/app.ts`.
- Wrap global middleware with `matchMiddleware()` to scope it to a path:

```ts
import { matchMiddleware } from "@ramonyx/server";

createHandler({
  middleware: [
    matchMiddleware("/admin/*", adminAudit),
    matchMiddleware(/^\/api\//, apiRateLimit),
    matchMiddleware((path) => path.endsWith(".json"), jsonHeaders),
  ],
});
```

Strings are exact paths, trailing `*` means prefix, RegExp is tested against the pathname, and a
function receives the pathname. Non-matching middleware calls `next()` with the current request.

```ts
export default [
  securityHeaders(),
  cspNonce(),
  rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowSeconds: 60 }),
];
```

## HTTP limits (secure by default)

| Limit | Default | On exceed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request body | 1 MiB | `413` |
| Handler/loader/render | 10 s | `503` + `request.signal` aborted |
| Concurrent requests | 100 | `503` + `Retry-After` |

Override per app via `createHandler({ maxBodyBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrent })`. Page actions also
accept `createPageRoutes({ maxBodyBytes })` (default 1 MiB) for streamed multipart/form bodies.

## Typed routes

`ramonyx build` and `ramonyx dev` generate `.ramonyx/routes.ts` with a typed `routeHref()` helper,
a generated `Link`, and a `RouteParamsMap`, so wrong paths or params fail at type-check time. Import
from the stable `#routes` alias configured by the template.

## i18n routing

`createPageRoutes({ i18n: { locales: ["en", "id"], defaultLocale: "en" } })` registers a route per
locale (`/id/...`), keeps the default locale unprefixed, sets `<html lang>` + `hreflang`, and
passes `locale` to loaders and page props. See the i18n section in the source docs for the full
guide (translation helper, negotiation, language switcher).

## docs/public/security/overview.md

# Security Overview

Ramonyx is designed to be **secure by default**: limits apply before your code runs, and security
primitives ship in the framework instead of being copy-pasted between apps.

> This page describes mitigations, not guarantees. Security claims without executable tests are not
> made (see the repository's evidence policy). Report vulnerabilities privately via
> [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/RamonyxJS/ramonyx/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Defaults that apply to every app

| Control | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Request body limit | 1 MiB → `413` (checked before routing, including streamed bodies) |
| Handler/loader/render timeout | 10 s → `503`, with `request.signal` aborted |
| Concurrent requests | 100 → `503` + `Retry-After` (load shedding) |
| SSR document size | 2 MiB → `500` |
| Client bundle boundary | `node:*` imports and `*.server.ts` modules are rejected/stubbed at build time |

All limits are configurable per app (`createHandler({ maxBodyBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrent })`).

## Security primitives

```ts
import {
  cspNonce,
  csrfProtection,
  rateLimit,
  securityHeaders,
} from "@ramonyx/security";

export default [
  securityHeaders(),        // CSP (with nonce), nosniff, referrer policy, frame-ancestors
  cspNonce(),               // per-request nonce injected into the hydration payload
  csrfProtection(),         // double-submit cookie (Web Crypto HMAC, constant-time compare)
  rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowSeconds: 60 }),  // per client; identity from the adapter
];
```

- **CSP nonce** — the nonce travels with the hydration payload, so inline scripts carry the same
  nonce the policy allows. No `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts.
- **CSRF** — double-submit cookie + header, signed with Web Crypto; compare in constant time.
  `trustProxy` is opt-in, so a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` cannot evade rate limits by default.
- **Sessions** — cookie parsing/serialization with safe defaults (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure),
  HMAC-signed values, and a small session helper (`read/commit/clear`).
- **Outbound fetch** — `guardedFetch` (from `@ramonyx/security/ssrf`) rejects private/loopback/
  link-local targets, validates every redirect hop, and **pins the resolved IP** so DNS rebinding
  cannot redirect a connection to an internal address.
- **Input validation** — Standard Schema at the trust boundary (params, query, body, form); invalid
  input returns `400` with field-level `issues` before your handler runs.
- **Output safety** — React escaping everywhere; raw HTML requires an explicit
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; server errors never leak stack traces in production.

## Server/client boundary

Server-only code belongs in `*.server.ts` modules. The build:

1. rejects `node:*` imports in page/layout modules (with a message pointing at the file),
2. replaces `*.server.ts` imports in the **client** bundle with a poison-pill stub,
3. scans the client output for leaked Node built-ins.

A secret placed in a plain shared module can still reach the client — keep secrets in
`*.server.ts` or server-only loaders and pass only what the UI needs.

## Runtime (experimental)

The Rust/V8 runtime is experimental. Its permission model is **deny-all by default**
(`--allow-read|write|net|env` opt-in), with worker/process isolation, resource quotas, and an
OS-level sandbox (Landlock) for plugins. It is not part of the production promise yet.

## Dependency & supply chain

- Lockfile committed; `pnpm audit --audit-level high` in CI and weekly.
- New versions must be at least **24 hours old** before adoption (`minimumReleaseAge`), reducing
  exposure to compromised fresh releases.
- npm releases are published from **verified tarballs** with **provenance** (build → verify →
  publish), guarded by tag↔version checks.

## Limitations (honest)

- Rate limiting and load shedding are process-local; multi-instance deployments need a shared
  store.
- CSP is wired through `@ramonyx/security`; if you replace it, you own the policy.
- CSRF protection covers double-submit verification and the hidden `_csrf` field for no-JS form
  flows; token rotation on action re-renders is automatic.
- The experimental runtime has not had an external security audit.

## docs/public/sessions-and-auth.md

# Sessions & Auth

Ramonyx ships **auth primitives**, not a turnkey user-management product: safe cookies, HMAC
signing, password hashing, user-store contracts/adapters, one-time reset/verification tokens,
OAuth/OIDC authorization-code + PKCE, role/permission authorization, server-side session stores,
and CSRF protection. Email delivery, provider-specific quirks, and account UI remain application
concerns.

## Cookies

```ts
import { parseCookies, serializeCookie, expireCookie } from "@ramonyx/security";

const cookies = parseCookies(request.headers.get("cookie"));
const header = serializeCookie("theme", "dark", { path: "/", sameSite: "lax" });
```

Defaults for session cookies are safe: `path=/`, `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite=lax`.
`expireCookie(name)` produces `Max-Age=0`.

## Signed values

```ts
import { signValue, verifyValue } from "@ramonyx/security";

const signed = await signValue("user-42", env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!);
const value = await verifyValue(signed, env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!); // string | null
```

HMAC-SHA256 via Web Crypto with a constant-time comparison. The secret must come from env/bindings
(never hard-coded).

## Password hashing

```ts
import { hashPassword, verifyPassword } from "@ramonyx/security";

const stored = await hashPassword("correct horse battery staple");
const valid = await verifyPassword(candidate, stored);
```

The default encoding is `pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<hash>` with a random salt and 210,000
iterations. Always return the same generic error for an unknown user and a wrong password, and
store the hash string (not the password) in your user store.

## User store

`UserStore` is the persistence contract for account data. The reference implementations are:

- `createMemoryUserStore()` — development/tests only.
- `createKeyValueUserStore(store)` — any `KeyValueStore` (Redis/KV/cache). It keeps username and
  email indexes; **the unique-index check is best-effort**, so a database with real unique
  constraints remains the right choice under concurrent registration.

```ts
import { createKeyValueUserStore } from "@ramonyx/security";

const users = createKeyValueUserStore(store);
const user = await users.create({ username: "rina", email: "rina@example.test" });
await users.update(user.id, { emailVerified: true });
```

A SQL adapter only needs to implement five methods: `getById`, `getByUsername`, `getByEmail`,
`create`, `update`, and `delete`. A minimal migration for a relational database:

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id            text PRIMARY KEY,
  username      text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  email         text UNIQUE,
  password_hash text,
  email_verified boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  roles         text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{user}'
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_username_lower ON users (lower(username));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_email_lower ON users (lower(email)) WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
```

Normalize usernames/emails before storing them. Never expose password hashes in serializers.

## Password reset and email verification

`createAuthTokens({ store })` issues cryptographically random, **one-time** tokens. Only a
SHA-256 hash is stored, with a TTL; consuming deletes the record atomically from the application's
point of view.

```ts
import { createAuthTokens, createMemoryStore } from "@ramonyx/security";

const tokens = createAuthTokens({ store: createMemoryStore() });
const raw = await tokens.issue(user.id, "reset", 15 * 60);
const userId = await tokens.consume(raw, "reset"); // string | null
```

Rules for the application flow:

- Return the **same generic response** whether the account exists or not.
- Send the raw token by email; never put it in logs, URLs indexed by search engines, or responses.
- Apply `rateLimit()` to request/consume endpoints and use a short TTL (for example 15 minutes).
- On reset, rotate/revoke active sessions and hash the new password with `hashPassword()`.
- Mark `emailVerified` only after consuming a `"verify"` token; do not trust a query-string email.

The reference HTTP tests cover generic reset responses, one-time use, password replacement, and
one-time email verification (`packages/security/test/auth-flow.test.ts`).

## OAuth / OIDC

`createOAuthClient()` implements the authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256), `state`, and a
`nonce`. It is provider-agnostic and fetches JSON; inject `fetch` in tests.

```ts
import { createOAuthClient, createOAuthAccountLinker } from "@ramonyx/security";

const oauth = createOAuthClient({
  clientId: env.get("OAUTH_CLIENT_ID")!,
  clientSecret: env.get("OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  authorizationEndpoint: "https://provider.example/authorize",
  tokenEndpoint: "https://provider.example/token",
  userInfoEndpoint: "https://provider.example/userinfo",
  redirectUri: "https://app.example/auth/callback",
  scopes: ["openid", "email"],
});

const authorization = await oauth.authorize();
// store authorization.state, authorization.nonce, authorization.codeVerifier in the session
```

On callback:

1. Compare the returned `state` with the stored value (constant-time comparison is preferred).
2. Exchange the code with `oauth.exchange(code, storedCodeVerifier)`.
3. If an ID token is present, validate its signature/issuer/audience/nonce with your provider's
   JWKS and OIDC library; this package deliberately does not embed a JWKS cache.
4. Link the external identity with `createOAuthAccountLinker({ store, users }).link(profile)`.

Account linking only auto-links an existing account by email when the provider asserts
`emailVerified === true`. Unverified email claims are not stored. Unlinking removes the
provider+subject link and leaves the local user intact. Provider callback URLs must be registered
exactly (scheme, host, path) and secrets must come from env/bindings. OAuth errors returned to the
browser are generic; log provider details server-side without tokens or authorization codes.

## Authorization

Authorization is deny-by-default and works for route middleware and action bodies:

```ts
import { authorizationGuard, createAuthorization } from "@ramonyx/security";

const authz = createAuthorization({
  roles: {
    admin: ["user:manage", "audit:read"],
    user: ["post:read"],
  },
});

export const middleware = authorizationGuard({
  authorization: authz,
  permission: "user:manage",
  subject: ({ request }) => sessionSubject(await readSession(request)),
});
```

Denied routes get a generic `403`; the default audit path logs permission + path (no PII). In an
action, either call `authz.assert(subject, "user:manage")` before mutating or wrap the action with
`authorizedAction()`:

```ts
import { authorizedAction } from "@ramonyx/security";

export const action = authorizedAction(
  {
    authorization: authz,
    permission: "user:manage",
    subject: async ({ request }) => sessionSubject(await readSession(request)),
    audit: ({ permission }) => metrics.increment("authz.denied", { permission }),
  },
  async ({ params }) => {
    await users.delete(params.id);
    return { message: "deleted" };
  },
);
```

Map `AuthorizationError` to the same generic response. Direct permissions are combined with role
grants; an unknown role or a missing subject grants nothing. Migrate from manual checks by
centralizing the role → permission table and passing a subject built from the server-side session,
never from request JSON.

## Sessions

`createSession()` supports two modes:

- **Stateless** (default): the signed cookie contains the JSON data. Suitable for small,
  non-secret data. Signed data is **not encrypted**.
- **Store-backed**: the cookie contains only a signed session ID; data lives in a
  `SessionStore`. This enables rotation and server-side revocation.
  `createKeyValueSessionStore(store)` adapts any `KeyValueStore` (Redis/KV/cache) to this
  contract.

```ts
import { createMemorySessionStore, createSession } from "@ramonyx/security";

const session = createSession({
  secret: env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!,
  store: createMemorySessionStore(), // use KV/Redis/DB in production
  cookie: { secure: true },
});

// read
const data = await session.read(request); // SessionData | null

// login: new ID (fixation protection) + fresh cookie
const cookie = await session.rotate(request, { user: "rina" });

// logout: delete the store record + expire cookie
const cleared = await session.revoke(request);
```

`commit()` creates a session without rotating an existing ID. On login, prefer `rotate()` so a
pre-login session ID cannot be reused (session fixation). `read()` rejects invalid signatures,
malformed data, and expired store records. The in-memory store is for development/tests; use a
shared store for multi-instance production.

Action results can return `headers`; `set-cookie` headers are applied to the re-render.

Rate limiting can share the same `KeyValueStore` via `rateLimit({ store })`; `increment` is used
for atomic fixed-window counters. See [State & Adapters](state-and-adapters.md) for lifecycle and
failure-mode guidance.

## CSRF

```ts
import { csrfProtection } from "@ramonyx/security";

export default [csrfProtection({ secure: true })];
```

Double-submit cookie:
- a safe request issues a token cookie when missing;
- JavaScript sends it in `x-csrf-token`;
- no-JS forms send the same token in a hidden `_csrf` field;
- state-changing requests without a matching token get `403`.

For a no-JS form, read the active token in the loader from the internal request header:

```ts
import { CSRF_REQUEST_HEADER } from "@ramonyx/security";

export async function loader({ request }) {
  return { csrfToken: request.headers.get(CSRF_REQUEST_HEADER) ?? "" };
}
```

```tsx
<form method="post">
  <input type="hidden" name="_csrf" value={data.csrfToken} />
  {/* fields */}
</form>
```

The active token is copied onto the request for action re-renders, so forms rendered after a
mutation remain valid. Form-field verification reads a clone of the request body; the action still
receives the original body.

## Reference flow

`apps/playground/src/routes/sesi` is an end-to-end reference: PBKDF2 password hashes, an in-memory
user/session store, login/logout/register, session rotation, CSRF for JS and no-JS forms, and a
basic rate limit. The tests cover both JavaScript and native form flows.

## Limitations (honest)

- Signed cookies are not encrypted; do not put secrets in stateless session data.
- The default session/user stores are in-memory; production deployments need shared stores and a
  secret-rotation strategy. The KeyValue user adapter's unique indexes are best-effort; use real
  database constraints under concurrent registration.
- Reset/verification email delivery and account UI are application concerns. Tokens are hashed and
  one-time, but the app must add generic responses, rate limits, and session revocation.
- OAuth/OIDC ID-token signature, issuer, audience, and nonce validation is delegated to the
  application/OIDC library; state and PKCE verifiers must be stored server-side per attempt.
- Authorization is a primitive, not a policy database or admin UI. Audit events must still be
  shipped to your logging/metrics backend.
- Rate limits are per-process unless a shared store with atomic `increment` is supplied.

## docs/public/ssr-hydration.md

# SSR & Hydration

Ramonyx renders pages on the server, sends a hydration payload, and hydrates the same React tree in
the browser. Streaming is opt-in.

## What a request looks like

```
Request → middleware → route match → loader → render (React) → HTML document → Response
```

The document contains:

- the server-rendered markup inside `#ramonyx-root`,
- `<script id="ramonyx-payload">window.__RAMONYX__ = { path, params, data, action, locale }</script>`,
- the hashed client bundle (`/assets/client-<hash>.js`) that hydrates the tree and wires soft
  navigation, prefetch, and form interception.

Because the payload is embedded, there is no extra data request on hydration.

## Streaming (opt-in)

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ app: { streaming: true } });
```

With `streaming: true`, the shell (head + layout) is sent immediately and the body is streamed with
`renderToReadableStream` (edge build of React). Errors after the first byte close the stream — the
status can no longer change. Error pages are always rendered synchronously.

## Layouts & error boundaries

- `layout.tsx` wraps pages in the folder and above; layouts receive `children`.
- `error.tsx` receives `{ error: { status, message, details? } }`. `details` (stack + source file)
  is only included outside production. Render the optional `DevErrorOverlay` to show a
  non-production overlay with the stack and a `vscode://file/...` link:

  ```tsx
  import { DevErrorOverlay } from "@ramonyx/react";

  {error.details === undefined ? null : <DevErrorOverlay details={error.details} />}
  ```

  The component is not injected automatically; a production error page that ignores `details`
  never renders it.
- Unknown paths fall through to a catch-all page (the template ships `[...slug]` with
  `metadata.status = 404`).

## Client behavior

| Feature | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Hydration | `hydrateRoot` on the existing markup; pages with islands hydrate only their marked boundaries |
| Deferred data | `defer()` + `<Suspense>` streams a server fallback, then the resolved boundary with a state script for hydration |
| Soft navigation | same-origin links fetch the next HTML, reconcile the head, swap the container, re-hydrate, `pushState` |
| Code splitting | client entry dynamically imports the active route/layout chunks; other routes load on navigation/prefetch |
| Prefetch | hover/focus/viewport prefetch HTML and warm the route chunk (LRU 8 entries, 30 s, max 2 concurrent) |
| Forms | submit intercepted when JS is available; `POST` + `303` PRG without JS |
| Scroll | `popstate` restores scroll; new navigations start at the top |

## Deferred loader data (streaming)

`defer()` starts non-critical work immediately and returns a thenable that can be read with
React's `use()` inside a `<Suspense>` boundary:

```tsx
import { defer, type Deferred } from "ramonyx";
import { Suspense, use } from "react";

export async function loader() {
  return {
    title: "Dashboard",
    stats: defer(() => loadStats()),
  };
}

function Stats({ value }: { value: Deferred<{ visits: number }> }) {
  const stats = use(value);
  return <p data-stats>{stats.visits} visits</p>;
}

export default function Dashboard({ data }: { data: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loader>> }) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{data.title}</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading stats…</p>}>
        <Stats value={data.stats} />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  );
}
```

- **Streaming is required** (`streaming: true`). The shell and a meaningful fallback are sent
  first; the resolved boundary follows and is revealed in the browser.
- **No-JS**: the fallback is the content users see. Make it useful (not an empty spinner); the
  final deferred value is progressively enhanced and is not available without JavaScript.
- The resolved values are serialized into a `<script type="application/json">` state tag after
  the mount container; the client reads it for hydration. Values must be JSON-serializable and
  must be rendered inside the boundary.
- **Soft navigation/actions** use a synchronous render; the client re-renders the deferred route
  from the state tag (avoiding React Suspense hydration mismatch). Prefetch, back/forward, and
  no-JS remain unchanged.
- A deferred rejection cannot change the response status after the first byte; React keeps the
  boundary fallback and switches it to client rendering, while `onError` logs the failure. Wrap
  recoverable failures with a React error boundary for a custom fallback.
- Deferred data is for non-critical UI. Keep critical content in the awaited loader result; do not
  combine deferred loader data with loader caching (`revalidate`).

## Code splitting & streaming boundaries

- The generated client entry uses dynamic imports per page/layout. The initial entry hydrates
  only the active route; other route chunks are loaded on navigation and warmed by prefetch.
- Streaming is active (`streaming: true`), but loaders resolve before render except data explicitly
  wrapped in `defer()`. Deferred boundaries are opt-in and retain a server-rendered fallback.
- Islands and deferred data are separate opt-ins. A page with islands hydrates only marked
  boundaries; a page with deferred data hydrates the route and client-renders it on soft
  navigation.

## Partial hydration islands (opt-in)

A page can mark interactive boundaries instead of hydrating the whole route. Register the client
component at module scope and render an `Island` with JSON-serializable props:

```tsx
import { defineIsland, Island } from "@ramonyx/react/islands";
import { useState } from "react";

function Counter({ start }: { start: number }) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(start);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount((value) => value + 1)}>Count: {count}</button>;
}

defineIsland("counter", Counter);

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <main>
      <p>Static server content.</p>
      <Island id="counter" props={{ start: 2 }} />
    </main>
  );
}
```

- The server renders the component inside a `data-ramonyx-island` wrapper. The client detects
  markers and calls `hydrateRoot` only on those wrappers; the rest of the route stays static.
- Detection is per page. **If a page contains any island, its whole route is island-hydrated** —
  every component that relies on React state, effects, or event props on that page or layout must
  be an `Island`. Document-level soft navigation and form interception still work for static
  markup.
- Island IDs are global and must be unique; props must be JSON-serializable (no functions,
  elements, `Date`/`Map`/`Set`, or circular references). Nested islands are not supported.
- Each island is an independent React root. React context from a static layout is not available;
  pass data through props or mount the provider inside the island. Shared state must live outside
  the island roots. React `useId` is supported because server and client use the same per-island
  identifier prefix.
- Soft navigation, prefetch, back/forward, and action re-renders hydrate the new page's islands;
  pages without islands keep the existing full-tree hydration. No-JS output is unchanged.
- Islands are a client-side boundary, not a server-component or data-loading feature.

## Soft navigation & head reconciliation

A soft navigation does not reload the document. Before the body is swapped, the client reconciles
the new document's head with the active one:

- `<title>` and `<html lang>`/`dir` are updated.
- `<meta>` and `<link>` tags are matched by their identity (`name`/`property`/`rel` + target);
  obsolete metadata and discovery links are removed.
- Inline `<style>` tags are staged with `media="not all"` and activated at the swap, so the old
  page keeps its styles until the new body is ready.
- External stylesheets are preloaded before the swap; the real `<link rel="stylesheet">` is then
  installed and the old styles/link are removed. The wait is capped at 2 seconds.
- New inline styles reuse the **current document's CSP nonce**, never the nonce embedded in the
  fetched document (the response's CSP header belongs to the active document).

The server document marks its generated style block with `data-ramonyx-style` so the client can
reconcile it without touching unrelated runtime nodes. Vite development styles are left alone.

### Boundaries

- `<script>` tags in the fetched head are not added or executed; the active client bundle remains
  responsible for navigation and hydration. Server-rendered payload data changes through
  `window.__RAMONYX__`, not through a new script.
- Nodes that are not part of the server head (for example Vite HMR styles) are preserved.
- Prefetch responses go through the same reconciliation path as normal navigation.
- If an external stylesheet fails to load, navigation continues after the timeout and falls back
  to the styles already in the document.

## Data loading & caching

Loaders run on the server on every request unless a page opts into caching:

```ts
export const revalidate = 60;                 // seconds (ISR-lite)
export const cacheTags = ["products"];        // for on-demand invalidation

export async function loader() {
  return { products: await db.products.list() };
}
```

- Responses that depend on a session (cookies) or query strings are **not** cached.
- Serve stale data while refreshing in the background (`stale-while-revalidate`).
- Invalidate on demand: `revalidate({ paths: ["/products"], tags: ["products"] })` from a loader,
  action (`context.revalidate`), or the cache instance.
- The default cache is in-memory per process; the store interface is pluggable for multi-instance
  deployments.

## Server actions

An `action` export turns a page into a mutation endpoint (POST to the same URL). It receives
`{ params, formData, request, env, log, locale, json(), revalidate() }` and can return
`{ message, errors, data, status, headers, redirect }`. A redirect is `303` (POST/Redirect/GET).

```ts
export async function action({ formData, revalidate }) {
  await db.notes.create({ text: String(formData.get("text") ?? "") });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["notes"] });
  return { message: "Saved" };
}
```

### Pending, optimistic UI, and declarative revalidation

`@ramonyx/react` provides small opt-in primitives for actions:

```tsx
import { PendingButton, useActionStatus, useOptimisticForm } from "@ramonyx/react";

const [optimistic, setOptimistic] = useOptimisticForm({ name: "" });

<form
  method="post"
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget);
    setOptimistic({ name: String(data.get("name") ?? "") });
  }}
>
  <input name="name" />
  <PendingButton pendingText="Saving…">Save</PendingButton>
</form>;

{optimistic.name ? <p>Optimistic: {optimistic.name}</p> : null}
```

- The client sets `aria-busy` on the form and dispatches `ramonyx:actionstart` /
  `ramonyx:actionend`; `useActionStatus()` (and `PendingButton`) follow those events.
- `useOptimisticForm()` keeps local optimistic values until the server action re-render replaces
  them with authoritative data.
- Native form POST still works with JavaScript disabled; these primitives simply do nothing.
- Page actions limit form bodies to `maxBodyBytes` (default 1 MiB) while streaming; oversized
  chunked/multipart uploads return `413` without buffering the whole body. Tune this independently
  from the API handler limit via `createPageRoutes({ maxBodyBytes })`.
- To invalidate other data after a successful action, declare it in the page module:

```ts
export const cacheTags = ["notes"];
export const actionRevalidate = { tags: ["notes"] };
```

The server invalidates those tags after a successful action (and fires `onInvalidate`); actions
that return `errors` do not invalidate. This complements `context.revalidate()` for action-local
logic.

## Related primitives

- `AppHooks` (`onRequestStart/End`, `onLoaderEnd`, `onRenderEnd`, `onInvalidate`) for instrumentation.
- `traceId()`, `requestLogging()`, `createMetrics()` from `@ramonyx/server` for observability.
- Asset resolver + `Image` for hashed assets, responsive images, and anti-CLS dimensions.

## docs/public/state-and-adapters.md

# State & Adapters

Ramonyx separates **state contracts** from implementations. The default implementations are
in-memory so a new app starts without infrastructure; production can swap in a shared store without
changing application code.

## Contracts

| Contract | Used by | Required behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KeyValueStore` / `CacheStore` | loader cache, revalidation | `get`, `set` with TTL/tags, `delete`, `invalidateTags`; optional atomic `take` and `increment` |
| `SessionStore` | `createSession({ store })` | `get`, `set`, `delete`; expiry is enforced by the store/cookie |
| `RateLimitStore` | `rateLimit({ store })` | atomic `increment(key, { windowSeconds })` |
| `ObservabilitySink` | `createMetrics({ sink })` | `record(event)`; must be fast and must not make requests fail |

In-memory references:

```ts
import {
  createMemoryStore,
  createMemoryObservabilitySink,
} from "ramonyx";
import { createMemorySessionStore } from "@ramonyx/security";

const store = createMemoryStore();                 // CacheStore + RateLimitStore
const sessions = createMemorySessionStore();       // SessionStore
const sink = createMemoryObservabilitySink();      // ObservabilitySink
```

The shared `KeyValueStore` contract is covered by `tests/contracts/store.contract.ts`; the
session/rate-limit/user/token adapters add their own focused tests.

## Lifetimes and failure modes

- **In-memory defaults are per process.** Multi-instance deployments must use a shared adapter;
  otherwise sessions, rate limits, and cache invalidation diverge between instances.
- **TTL is owned by the store.** Framework entries carry an absolute `expiresAt` where relevant,
  but adapters must honor `ttlSeconds`. Clock skew between application and store shifts expiry.
- **Atomic operations are explicit.** `increment` must be atomic for rate limiting; `take` must be
  atomic for one-time tokens. `createAuthTokens` uses `take` when available and documents the
  best-effort fallback for older adapters.
- **Fail fast, do not silently fall back.** A store outage should surface as an error, not switch
  to process-local state (which would silently weaken sessions/limits). The observability sink is
  the exception: `createMetrics` swallows sink errors so a collector outage cannot break traffic.
- **No automatic retries for non-idempotent operations.** Retrying an increment can over-count;
  retries/timeouts belong to the adapter with operation-aware semantics.
- **Cache tags are indexes.** `invalidateTags` must remove matching entries and their index
  references, otherwise deleted data remains reachable by the next tag invalidation.

## Observability sink

```ts
import { createJsonObservabilitySink } from "ramonyx";
import { createMetrics } from "@ramonyx/server";

const metrics = createMetrics({
  sink: createJsonObservabilitySink((line) => process.stdout.write(line)),
});
```

Events are `request.end`, `loader.end`, `render.end`, and `cache.invalidate`, with primitive
attributes (path, status, duration, cached, streaming, invalidation reason/tags). JSON-lines is
directly consumable by OTel/Fluent Bit/Vector agents; an OTel SDK exporter can implement the same
`ObservabilitySink` interface.

Sinks should enqueue or write non-blocking. Hooks are synchronous and must stay cheap; do not call
a remote collector inline.

## Wiring a shared adapter

```ts
import { createCache } from "ramonyx";
import {
  createKeyValueSessionStore,
  createKeyValueUserStore,
  rateLimit,
} from "@ramonyx/security";

const cache = createCache({ store });                       // KeyValueStore
const session = createSession({ secret, store: createKeyValueSessionStore(store) });
const users = createKeyValueUserStore(store);
const limiter = rateLimit({ limit: 60, windowMs: 60_000, store });
```

`store` is any object satisfying `KeyValueStore`. Redis/KV adapters still need to provide TTL,
atomic increment, atomic take, tag indexes, reconnect behavior, and deployment-specific failure
handling; those production adapters are tracked separately from the in-memory contract.

## Redis adapter (Node)

`@ramonyx/adapter-runtime` provides a Redis-backed `KeyValueStore` for Node deployments:

```ts
import { connectRedisStore } from "@ramonyx/adapter-runtime";

const redis = await connectRedisStore({
  url: env.get("REDIS_URL")!,
  prefix: "app:",
  onError: (error) => logger.error("redis", { error: error.message }),
});
try {
  const cache = createCache({ store: redis.store });
  const session = createSession({
    secret: env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!,
    store: createKeyValueSessionStore(redis.store),
  });
  const limiter = rateLimit({ limit: 60, windowMs: 60_000, store: redis.store });
  // ...serve
} finally {
  await redis.close();
}
```

Behavior:

- Values are JSON envelopes; TTL uses Redis `SET EX` and tag membership uses Redis sets.
- `increment` and one-time `take` use Lua scripts so two instances cannot both succeed.
- `connectRedisStore` enables node-redis reconnect with capped exponential backoff. Errors are
  surfaced through `onError` and operations reject; there is **no local fallback** that would
  silently split sessions/limits between processes.
- The adapter is Node-only and lives in `@ramonyx/adapter-runtime`; the core/security contracts
  remain edge-safe. Cloudflare KV and other eventually-consistent stores do not provide atomic
  increment/take, so they need a purpose-built adapter rather than pretending to satisfy
  `RateLimitStore`/one-time-token semantics.
- Prefixes isolate applications sharing one Redis database. Tag sets are cleaned on delete/take and
  lazily cleaned during invalidation.

The integration test starts a local `redis-server`, uses two independent connections, and verifies
shared sessions, shared rate limits, atomic one-time tokens, cache invalidation, TTL, and fail-fast
error propagation. It is skipped when `redis-server` is unavailable.

## Defaults in examples

The playground and templates keep the in-memory adapters, so `pnpm dev` and `pnpm build` work
without Redis or a database. Opt in to shared adapters only when the deployment is multi-instance.

## docs/public/testing.md

# Testing

Test the handler in-process (no ports, no runtime), then add browser tests for hydration and
progressive enhancement.

## In-process tests

`@ramonyx/testing` wraps a handler in an in-memory host:

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { createTestServerFromHandler } from "@ramonyx/testing";
import { createApp } from "../src/app.ts";

test("GET / renders SSR", async () => {
  const server = await createTestServerFromHandler(await createApp());
  try {
    const response = await server.fetch("/");
    assert.equal(response.status, 200);
    assert.match(await response.text(), /Hello/);
  } finally {
    await server.close();
  }
});
```

- `createTestServerFromHandler(handler)` — any `FetchHandler` (e.g. from `createApp`).
- `createTestServer({ routes, middleware })` — build a handler from route entries directly.
- `server.fetch(path | Request, init?)` resolves relative URLs against the in-memory origin.
- **Always `close()` in `finally`** — a leaked listener makes `node --test` hang.

## What to test

| Layer | Approach |
| --- | --- |
| Routing / params / methods | `server.fetch` — assert `200`, `404`, `405` + `Allow` |
| Validation | invalid query/params/body → `400` with `issues` |
| Loaders & actions | assert rendered HTML and the hydration payload |
| Cache/revalidate | call twice, assert loader counts and stale-while-revalidate behavior |
| Security | body limits (`413`), timeout (`503`), concurrency (`503` + `Retry-After`), CSRF |
| Browser | Playwright: hydration, soft navigation, forms with and without JS |

## Browser tests

The repo's playground runs Playwright against a production build (`pnpm build && pnpm test:e2e`).
For a new app:

```ts
// e2e/home.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";

test("hydrates and handles a form", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: /Click/ }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("button")).toHaveText(/1/);
});
```

Test **no-JS** by disabling JavaScript in the Playwright context: forms must still submit
(`POST` + `303` PRG).

## Commands

```bash
pnpm test          # node --test (packages, apps, tests, benchmarks)
pnpm test:e2e      # Playwright against a production build
pnpm test:docs     # this site's e2e (policy + a11y), if you vendor the docs app
```

## Tips

- Loader data must be JSON-serializable — assert the payload shape when in doubt.
- Use a fresh app/server per test for isolation; keep shared fixtures read-only.
- The dev scripts run app TypeScript/JSX through `@ramonyx/compiler/register` (no build step).

## docs/public/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Framework errors carry a stable code and a link to this page. Search the code below, or grab the
anchor from the error message.

## RMX-CONFIG-1 — invalid config

`ramonyx.config.ts` has a value with the wrong type.

| Field | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `app.strictValidation` | boolean |
| `app.streaming` | boolean |
| `server.port` | integer 0–65535 |
| `server.host` | non-empty string |

Fix the value; unknown keys are kept (config pass-through) and are not the cause.

## RMX-APP-1 — missing server entry

The CLI/check could not find `src/app.ts` (must export `createApp(options?)`) or `src/server.ts`
(must export `createHandler(options?)`). Create the missing entry, or pass the correct app
directory with `--app`.

## RMX-CHECK-1 — unexpected check failure

`ramonyx check` failed before it could classify the problem. The message is the original error;
run `ramonyx doctor` and check the config/route files. This usually means a module threw while
being imported.

## RMX-ROUTES-1 — can't read the routes directory

The compiler cannot read `src/routes` (missing directory or permissions). Create
`src/routes/page.tsx` or point the CLI at the right app with `--app`.

## RMX-ROUTES-2 — missing default export

A page/layout/error module has no `default` export. Every `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, and `error.tsx`
must export the component as default:

```tsx
export default function Page() { /* ... */ }
```

## RMX-ROUTES-3 — invalid middleware export

A `middleware.ts` must default-export an **array of functions**:

```ts
import type { Middleware } from "ramonyx";
export default [securityHeaders(), cspNonce()] satisfies Middleware[];
```

## RMX-ROUTES-4 — API route without an HTTP method export

An `api/**/*.ts` file exports none of `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS`. Export at
least one using `route({ handler })`.

## RMX-ROUTES-5 — invalid route definition

An exported method is not a route definition. Use the helper:

```ts
export const GET = route({
  handler: ({ json }) => json({ ok: true }),
});
```

## RMX-BUILD-1 — server import in a client module

A page/layout imports `node:*` directly. The client bundle cannot contain Node APIs. Move that code
into a `*.server.ts` module and call it from a loader/action/API route; the client bundle gets a
poison-pill stub instead of your server code.

## RMX-BUILD-2 — server code leaked into the client bundle

Same problem, but through a transitive import (or a Vite browser-external shim was found). Split the
server-only code behind `*.server.ts` and import it only from the server side.

## RMX-EDGE-1 — `node:*` in the edge artifact

The edge target rejects Node built-ins. `guardedFetch` lives in a Node-only subpath; import it from
`@ramonyx/security/ssrf` **only** in Node code, and keep edge code on `fetch`.

## Common non-coded issues

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `413` on POST | Body over 1 MiB. Raise `maxBodyBytes` in `createHandler` or stream/upload differently. |
| `503` after 10 s | Handler/loader/render timeout. Optimize, or raise `timeoutMs`. `request.signal` is aborted. |
| `503` + `Retry-After` under load | Concurrency limit (default 100) shedding load. Scale out or raise `maxConcurrent`. |
| Hydration mismatch / no interactivity | Client bundle not built (`ramonyx build` before `ramonyx start`) or an error page (error pages are not hydrated). |
| Assets 404 in production | Build first; assets are hashed into `dist/client` and served by `ramonyx start`. |
| `node_modules` TypeScript fails | Node does not type-strip `node_modules`; publish compiled JS for plugins/consumers. |
| Dev server panel missing | Open the URL printed by `ramonyx dev` (`/__ramonyx/devtools`); it is dev-only. |

## Getting more detail

- Development error pages include the stack and source file; production pages never do.
- The CLI `ramonyx doctor` prints config, route count, and build status.
- See [Testing](testing.md) for reproducing issues in-process.


## Client/server boundaries

`ramonyx build` (and `buildClient`) statically rejects page/layout/error modules that import
`node:*`, `server-only`, or `*.server.ts`, before Vite attempts the bundle. Move database/secrets
code into a `*.server.ts` module and import it only from a loader, action, or API route. The error
names the offending file and specifier; the compiler also exposes `lintClientBoundaries(pages)` if
you want the check in your own tooling.

## docs/public/typed-routes.md

# Typed Routes

`ramonyx build` and `ramonyx dev` generate `.ramonyx/routes.ts` from your page manifest. Use it to
make route paths and params type-safe at compile time.

## Generated module

```ts
// .ramonyx/routes.ts (generated — do not edit)
export type RouteParamsMap = {
  "/": undefined;
  "/users": undefined;
  "/users/[id]": { id: string };
  "/blog/[...slug]": { slug: string };
};

export function routeHref<P extends keyof RouteParamsMap>(
  path: P,
  ...args: RouteParamsMap[P] extends undefined ? [] : [params: RouteParamsMap[P]]
): string;

export const Link = createLink<RouteParamsMap>();
```

The template and playground map `#routes` to the generated file in both TypeScript and Node
(`package.json#imports`), so use the stable alias:

```tsx
import { Link, routeHref } from "#routes";

routeHref("/users");                    // "/users"
routeHref("/users/[id]", { id: "42" }); // "/users/42"
<Link href="/users/[id]" params={{ id: "42" }}>User 42</Link>;
```

Wrong paths, missing dynamic params, or params on a static route fail at type-check time. The
generated file is refreshed on `ramonyx dev` and `ramonyx build` — no manual step. Existing apps
can add the same `#routes` mapping; the generated module is app-local, so it cannot be shipped as
a fixed package path.

## `Link` component

`Link` from `@ramonyx/react/link` renders an `<a>` and uses the client navigation/prefetch path.
For typed routes, use the generated `Link` above (it calls `createLink` and fills params). The
low-level `createLink` is exported if you need a custom route map.

```tsx
import { createLink } from "@ramonyx/react/link";

const Link = createLink<{ "/": undefined; "/users/[id]": { id: string } }>();
<Link href="/users/[id]" params={{ id: "42" }}>User 42</Link>;
```

## Notes

- The module only exists after the first `build`/`dev` run.
- Use the `#routes` alias from the template; it is configured for TypeScript and Node/Vite.
- The params map follows the file router: `[param]` → required single segment, `[...param]` → rest.
- Custom codegen? The manifest is the source; `generateRouteTypes(pages)` is exported from
  `@ramonyx/compiler` if you need it in another tool.

## Experimental runtime (Rust + V8)

Permission deny-all model, HTTP server with streaming/cancellation, worker and process isolation,
CPU/RSS quotas, plugin sandbox (Landlock), TLS `fetch`, CommonJS interop. Shipped as a separate
binary; **not part of the production promise** yet — see the repository for its assessments.
